papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Optimal treatment for synchronous brain metastases at lung cancer diagnosis depends on subtype, but histologic/molecular profiling is often delayed. We developed machine-learning models using clinical and imaging data to classify lung cancer into three subtypes with distinct brain metastasis treatment implications: small cell lung cancer (SCLC), EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (EGFR+), and EGFR-wild-type non-small cell lung cancer (EGFR-). METHODS: We retrospectively identified patients with metastatic lung cancer diagnosed from 2016 to 2025 at a single institution. Patients without brain metastases at diagnosis formed the training cohort, while patients presenting with synchronous brain metastases formed the testing cohort. Clinical variables and thoracic imaging features from diagnostic chest CT reports were used to train LASSO logistic regression and random forest models, evaluated via AUC and standard diagnostic metrics. Feature contributions were assessed using logistic regression coefficients and random forest permutation importance. RESULTS: Of 305 patients, 182 were used for training and 123 comprised the testing cohort. Logistic regression achieved AUCs of 0.887, 0.811, and 0.801 for EGFR+, SCLC, and EGFR-, respectively; random forest achieved 0.907, 0.783, and 0.810. Adding imaging features to clinical variables improved prediction for EGFR + and SCLC. Contributory imaging features included fibrosis, emphysema, miliary pattern, cavitation, pleural attachment, and vessel encasement, among others. Three-way prediction showed highest positive predictive value for EGFR + and high negative predictive value for SCLC. CONCLUSION: Combined clinical and chest imaging features can help predict lung cancer subtype, supporting early multidisciplinary discussions for patients with synchronous brain metastases.

papers.abstract_en: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is a promising biomarker for disease monitoring, yet evidence of its clinical utility in routine care remains limited. We evaluated the utility of serial ctDNA monitoring using digital PCR (ddPCR) for detecting acquired resistance (AR) and monitoring response in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and breast cancer (MBC). This real-world, longitudinal study included 48 metastatic patients (42 with EGFR-mutant NSCLC; 6 with HR+/HER2-negative MBC) treated at a Brazilian oncology reference center. Serial plasma samples were analyzed by ddPCR for activating and resistance mutations at specific time points. In the NSCLC cohort, EGFR T790M was detected in 48.4% of patients who progressed on 1st/2nd-generation TKIs. For patients on 3rd-generation TKIs, EGFR C797S was the main AR mechanism (47%), followed by PIK3CA, BRAF mutations, and ERBB2/EGFR amplifications. Longitudinal analysis anticipated radiological progression by approximately 5 months. Early molecular response, characterized by mutation clearance, preceded radiological response. In the MBC cohort, hotspot ESR1 mutations (D538G, L536R, Y537S) were identified in 50% of patients. Variations in ctDNA fractional abundance predicted disease progression up to 9 months before radiological confirmation. This study provides real-world evidence that ddPCR-based ctDNA monitoring enables early detection of resistance and predicts disease progression significantly earlier than standard imaging in both NSCLC and MBC. Despite the limited sample size, particularly in the MBC cohort, these real-world findings support liquid biopsy as a minimally invasive tool with the potential to guide therapeutic decisions and inform personalized management in precision oncology. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these observations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Evidence on the associations of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) intake and sleep patterns with lung cancer remains inconsistent. We aimed to examine these associations in southwest China and to explore whether the association between sleep patterns and lung cancer differed according to dietary PUFA intake. METHODS: We conducted a matched case-control study in Chongqing, southwest China, from August 22, 2023, to September 30, 2024. Each lung cancer case was matched to two controls by age group (<45, 45-65, or >65 years) and sex. Dietary PUFA intake was assessed using a validated semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (SQFFQ), and sleep patterns were evaluated using a composite healthy sleep score based on five sleep characteristics. Multivariable conditional logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: A total of 322 lung cancer cases and 644 matched controls were included. In continuous analyses, each 1-g/day increase in omega-3 PUFA intake was associated with lower odds of lung cancer (OR = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.70-0.96). In tertile-based analyses, participants in the highest versus lowest intake tertiles had lower odds of lung cancer across all three PUFA types (omega-3 PUFAs: OR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.32-0.78; omega-6 PUFAs: OR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.31-0.80; total PUFAs: OR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.30-0.79). Favorable sleep patterns were also associated with lower odds of lung cancer compared with unfavorable sleep patterns (OR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.40-0.87). Although lower stratum-specific ORs were observed in the higher omega-3 PUFA intake stratum, the multiplicative interaction tests were not statistically significant. CONCLUSION: Higher dietary omega-3 PUFA intake and favorable sleep patterns were each associated with lower odds of lung cancer in this matched case-control study. Associations for omega-6 and total PUFA intake were observed in tertile-based analyses but were not consistent across modeling approaches. These observational findings require confirmation in prospective studies.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS/BACKGROUND: Lung cancer patients undergoing combined chemoradiotherapy often experience pain, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and decreased quality of life. Among these, pain catastrophizing, as a negative cognitive pattern, can exacerbate symptom experience. Similarly, fatigue and sleep disturbances are also influenced by psychological and cognitive factors, yet conventional supportive care provides limited intervention at the psychological and cognitive levels. This study aims to investigate the impact of electromyographic biofeedback relaxation training on pain catastrophizing and fatigue levels in lung cancer patients undergoing combined chemoradiotherapy. METHODS: This study employed a single-center, retrospective cohort design. Through a review of medical records from March 2020 to March 2022, patients who had received structured electromyographic biofeedback relaxation training undergoing chemoradiotherapy were assigned to an observation group (n = 78). Patients without such records, receiving only routine supportive care, were classified as a control group (n = 109). The training consisted of six sessions over two weeks. Outcomes, including pain catastrophizing (Pain Catastrophizing Scale), pain intensity (Visual Analogue Scale), sleep quality (European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer), and quality of life (Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue), were assessed before and after the intervention period. RESULTS: After the intervention, the pain catastrophism scores, pain intensity scores, and sleep disturbance scores of the observation group were significantly lower than those of the control group, while the fatigue score was significantly higher than that of the control group (all p < 0.05). Furthermore, the observation group also showed significantly better scores and total scores on multiple dimensions of quality of life (including physical well-being, social/family well-being, emotional health, functional well-being, and fatigue subscales) than the control group (p < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Supplementing routine combined chemoradiotherapy management with electromyographic biofeedback relaxation training was associated with lower levels of pain catastrophizing and fatigue, improved sleep quality, and enhanced overall quality of life in lung cancer patients. This intervention may represent a safe and feasible non-pharmacological support strategy for symptom management in lung cancer patients undergoing combined chemoradiotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cancer cachexia is a wasting disease characterized by changes in metabolism, muscle and weight loss, inadequate food intake, and functional decline. The disease affects 30%-50% of patients with solid tumors. There is limited literature describing the relationship between cachexia and health care resource utilization (HRU) and costs in the United States. OBJECTIVE: To compare the HRU and direct health plan costs for patients with colorectal, lung, and pancreatic cancer with and without a cachexia-associated diagnosis. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study in Merative MarketScan commercial and Medicare claims databases. Patients with cachexia-associated diagnoses were identified following a colorectal, lung, or pancreatic cancer diagnosis between October 1, 2016, and December 31, 2022. Patients without a cachexia-associated diagnosis were propensity score-matched 2:1 to patients with a cachexia-associated diagnosis. Average 1-year HRU and direct health plan costs were calculated using a modified Kaplan-Meier sample average approach to account for patients lost to follow-up before the end of the 1-year observation period. The significance of group differences was assessed by nonoverlapping bootstrap 95% CIs. RESULTS: The matched sample included 10,445 patients with a cachexia-associated diagnosis and 20,890 without across colorectal, lung, and pancreatic cancers. One-year health care costs were significantly higher for patients with a cachexia-associated diagnosis ($123,092; 95% CI = $119,664-$126,557) than for those without ($88,959; 95% CI = $86,964-$91,022). Patients with cachexia-associated diagnoses had significantly greater HRU than those without cachexia-associated diagnoses, including higher average 1-year hospital admissions (1.50; 95% CI = 1.47-1.53 vs 0.99; 95% CI = 0.97-1.01), emergency department visits (1.46; 95% CI = 1.42-1.50 vs 0.96; 95% CI = 0.93-0.98), outpatient visits (15.49; 95% CI = 15.15-15.83 vs 14.24; 95% CI = 14.02-14.46), and prescription fills (26.83; 95% CI = 26.31-27.35 vs 24.46; 95% CI = 24.11-24.80). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with colorectal, lung, and pancreatic cancer and cachexia-associated diagnoses had substantially higher 1-year HRU and cost of care compared with patients with cancer without cachexia-associated diagnoses. Our results highlight evidence of clinical and economic burden associated with cachexia-associated diagnoses in the US health care system.

Prompted awareness of 'persistent cough' remained similar, increasing from 109 (73.6%) to 121 (80.7%), which was not statistically significant. DISCUSSION: These unexpected findings may reflect methodological limitations and limited follow-up duration. They underscore the need for multi-model campaigns to improve symptom awareness and help-seeking behaviour. papers.abstract_en: Joint modeling (JM) of longitudinal and time-to-event (TTE) data is a powerful statistical technique that elucidates how temporal changes in a biomarker relate to TTE outcomes while accounting for study confounders. The growing use of next-generation sequencing (NGS) in precision oncology, particularly in capturing circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) methylation via liquid biopsy, offers new opportunities to apply JM for patient prognostication. In this study, we used JM to analyze a prospective cohort of 251 non-small cell lung cancer patients receiving standard-of-care immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment regimens. The JM is comprised of two sub-models-a hierarchical cubic spline random effects model for the longitudinal biomarker component and a Cox proportional hazards model for the TTE outcome component. Each sub-model incorporated baseline factors of age, gender, smoking status, and cancer stage. The main objective was to establish whether the evolution of a methylation-derived tumor fraction (TF) is associated with patient outcomes. Our investigation revealed that TF is strongly associated with both real-world overall survival and real-world progression-free survival. These results enable the generation of various patient-level predictions that capture the dynamic interplay between TF and patient outcomes, offering a path toward real-time, personalized prognostication. Although validation in larger, multi-center cohorts is needed before routine adoption, this work represents an important step toward integrating dynamic predictions into serial liquid biopsy monitoring. This approach demonstrates the potential of JM to provide more nuanced and adaptive disease evolution monitoring, offering better clinical decision guidance compared to static models or imaging alone.

papers.abstract_en: Inducing cuproptosis is considered a novel strategy to impede non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) progression. ATOX1 suppressed cuproptosis by chelating free copper ions. This study seeks to elucidate the pathways that regulate ATOX1 upstream and thereby pinpoint molecular targets for activating cuproptosis in NSCLC. Cuproptosis was induced with ES-Cu. Malignant phenotypes were assessed using CCK-8, clonogenic, and Transwell assays. RNA immunoprecipitation, RNA pull-down, and actinomycin D chase were used to examine IGF2BP2-ATOX1 mRNA interaction and mRNA stability. Protein-protein interactions and ubiquitination were examined by co-immunoprecipitation. The co-localization of USP11 and IGF2BP2 was visualized by immunofluorescence. IGF2BP2 protein stability was assessed following cycloheximide treatment. Copper content was quantified using a commercial kit. Gene and protein levels were evaluated by RT-qPCR and Western blot. RNA-binding domain mutant rescue experiments were conducted to determine the functional requirement of IGF2BP2 KH domains. A subcutaneous xenograft model was established to validate the regulatory axis in vivo. ATOX1 suppressed cuproptosis to support NSCLC proliferation. IGF2BP2 bound to the CDS of ATOX1 mRNA via the m6A site at position 261, thereby enhancing ATOX1 mRNA stability. The KH3-4 domains of IGF2BP2 were indispensable for this regulation. Upregulation of ATOX1 by IGF2BP2 inhibited cuproptosis and consequently drove NSCLC proliferation. USP11 maintained IGF2BP2 protein stability via deubiquitination, leading to suppression of cuproptosis and promotion of NSCLC progression through the IGF2BP2/ATOX1 axis in vitro. In vivo, the USP11-IGF2BP2-ATOX1 axis might promote NSCLC tumor growth by suppressing cuproptosis. USP11‑dependent deubiquitination stabilized IGF2BP2, which subsequently increased ATOX1 mRNA stability in an m6A‑dependent manner. Elevated ATOX1 expression inhibited cuproptosis and thereby accelerated NSCLC progression.

papers.abstract_en: SETD2 is a critical tumor suppressor in lung cancer that catalyzes histone H3 lysine 36 (H3K36) trimethylation. Oncogenic histone H3 alleles, including H3K36M, causally drive cancer formation by dominantly inhibiting SETD2 and other H3K36 methyltransferases. Here we show that expression of the H3K36M oncogene paradoxically suppresses tumor growth in KRAS-driven lung cancer by promoting transcription of repetitive elements and accumulation of cytoplasmic dsRNA, activating antiviral-like immune clearance. Unexpectedly, all attendant effects of H3K36M expression require SETD2 activity despite widespread loss of H3K36 trimethylation. Reducing H3K36 dimethylation through genetic or pharmacologic attenuation of NSD2 phenocopies H3K36M expression, revealing NSD2 as the relevant target through which H3K36M triggers immune activation. Mechanistically, H3K36M expression or NSD2 attenuation reveals a SETD2-dependent mechanism that limits EZH2-mediated repression of repetitive elements, enabling dsRNA accumulation and immune activation. These findings establish opposing roles for NSD2- and SETD2-dependent H3K36 methylation in lung tumor immunity and reveal an NSD2-SETD2-EZH2 axis that can be targeted to modulate viral mimicry and immune surveillance in cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immunotherapy has transformed the treatment landscape for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet resistance mediated by the tumor microenvironment (TME) limits its efficacy in most patients. This review aims to synthesize the current understanding of the TME as an integrated network driving immunotherapy resistance and to evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies aimed at overcoming it. METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive narrative review of key literature in the field, sourced from PubMed and major conference proceedings. The focus was on mechanistic studies elucidating immunosuppressive cell circuits, metabolic reprogramming, epigenetic regulation, spatial heterogeneity, and microbiome interactions within the lung cancer TME. Preclinical and clinical evidence for TME-targeted combination therapies and biomarker development was also critically analyzed. RESULTS: The TME orchestrates resistance through highly interconnected axes: (1) cellular circuits including myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), regulatory T cells (Tregs), and M2-polarized tumor-associated macrophages (M2-TAMs), (2) metabolic barriers (lactate acidosis, nutrient depletion), (3) epigenetic reprogramming, and (4) systemic communication via exosomes and the microbiome. Spatial transcriptomics reveals that driver mutations (e.g., EGFR, KRAS) shape distinct immune-excluded architectures. To disrupt this network, rational combination strategies-such as immune checkpoint inhibitors with metabolic modulators (LDHAi), epigenetic drugs, targeted agents (METi), or microbiome interventions-show synergistic potential in early-phase trials. Furthermore, a tiered biomarker system integrating spatial, metabolic, and microbial features is proposed to guide patient stratification. CONCLUSION: Overcoming immunotherapy resistance requires a paradigm shift from single-target to network-targeted therapy. This review provides an integrated framework for understanding TME-mediated resistance and translates these insights into a roadmap for clinical translation. Future efforts must prioritize biomarker-validated, rationally designed combination therapies to improve outcomes for patients with resistant NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with an unfavorable prognosis, and the molecular mechanisms underlying its metastatic progression remain incompletely defined. Here, we investigated the functional role of ephrin type-B receptor 1 (EPHB1), a member of the ephrin receptor family, in ESCC metastasis. Integrated analyses of RNA-sequencing data and publicly available databases demonstrated that EPHB1 expression is significantly upregulated in ESCC tissues and is positively associated with advanced tumor grade and poor patient survival. Gain- and loss-of-function assays revealed that EPHB1 knockdown markedly inhibited ESCC cell migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), whereas EPHB1 overexpression exerted the opposite effects. Consistently, in vivo metastasis assays further confirmed that EPHB1 promotes lung metastasis of ESCC cells. Mechanistically, we identified SRY-box transcription factor 2 (SOX2) as a critical upstream regulator that directly binds to the EPHB1 promoter and transcriptionally activates its expression. Rescue experiments demonstrated that SOX2-induced EMT and invasive capacity are largely mediated through EPHB1. Collectively, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized SOX2/EPHB1 signaling axis that drives ESCC metastasis and suggest EPHB1 as a potential therapeutic target for ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: Non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by marked spatial immune heterogeneity, commonly manifested as immune‑desert, immune‑excluded and immune‑inflamed phenotypes. These phenotypes are closely associated with variable responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Emerging evidence suggests that they are shaped not only by canonical immune pathways but also by mitochondrial processes that regulate immune priming, T‑cell trafficking and the maintenance of effector function. The present review summarizes how mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial DNA‑cGAS‑STING signaling, pathways mediated by tricarboxylic acid cycle metabolites, and non‑cell‑autonomous mitochondrial transfer may contribute to the establishment and maintenance of distinct spatial immune phenotypes in NSCLC. It is proposed that insufficient activation of innate immunity and impaired dendritic cell priming are particularly relevant to immune‑desert tumors, whereas chronic oxidative stress may reinforce barriers mediated by cancer‑associated fibroblasts (CAFs), transforming growth factor β, and the extracellular matrix in immune‑excluded tumors. By contrast, immune‑inflamed tumors may represent a state in which pre‑existing immune circuitry remains intact and tumor‑infiltrating lymphocytes retain greater mitochondrial fitness and metabolic resilience. The implications of these mechanisms for ICI sensitivity and cold‑to‑hot tumor conversion strategies were further discussed. Current evidence from human studies remains largely correlative, and prospective, spatially resolved functional studies are needed. Nevertheless, integrating mitochondrial biology with spatial immune architecture within a phenotype‑guided framework may generate testable hypotheses for future biomarker development and combination strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Objective.To develop a conditional vector-quantized (VQ) diffusion-based dynamic cone beam computed tomography imaging framework using dual-view x-ray projections for accurate reconstruction of respiratory-induced lung tumor motion, with the potential to enable four-dimensional (4D) target verification during lung radiotherapy.Methods.Patient-specific respiratory motion models were constructed from planning 4D- computed tomography(CT) images using deformable image registration and principal component analysis (PCA). Synthetic DVFs were generated by sampling PCA coefficients and applied to the reference-phase CT images to produce dynamic three-dimensional (3D) volumes, from which paired dual-view DRRs were generated. A conditional VQ diffusion framework was developed, consisting of separate two-dimensional and 3D vector quantized variational autoencoder s for encoding DRRs and DVFs into discrete latent representations, followed by a conditional diffusion model to learn the mapping from x-ray projection features to deformation vector field (DVF) latent representations. During inference, dual-view x-ray projections were encoded and processed by the conditional diffusion model to estimate DVFs, which were then used to deform the reference CT image and reconstruct temporally resolved 3D volumes.Results.The simulation study demonstrates that the estimated DVFs effectively captured the respiratory-induced deformation of lung tumors, and the reconstructed dynamic volume CT images demonstrated accurate anatomical motion characteristics across respiratory phases.Conclusion.The proposed patient-specific VQ diffusion framework enables accurate estimation of respiratory-induced lung tumor motion from dual-view x-ray projections and facilitates the high-temporal-resolution dynamic volume CT reconstruction. The results demonstrate its potential as an image-guided solution for tumor motion tracking in lung tumor radiotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are critical drivers of tumor progression and therapeutic resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, how CSCs remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) of NSCLC remains largely unclear. METHODS: Flow cytometry was performed to evaluate the immunomodulatory effects of NSCLC CSCs on T cell differentiation. RNA-sequencing-based metabolic profiling was conducted to identify pivotal metabolic pathways activated in CSCs. Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) encapsulated in CSC-derived exosomes were quantified, and the molecular mechanism by which exosomal ROS modulates intracellular nitric oxide (NO) production and FoxP3 post-translational modifications in T cells was further explored. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) were utilized as a preclinical model to verify the therapeutic potential of glutamine metabolism targeting. RESULTS: NSCLC CSCs potently induced tumor immunosuppression by promoting regulatory T (Treg) cell differentiation. Mechanistically, hyperactive glutamine metabolism in CSCs substantially increased mitochondrial ROS generation. Exosomal ROS secreted by CSCs was transferred to T cells, thereby elevating intracellular NO synthesis. Increased NO further triggered S-nitrosylation and deubiquitination of FoxP3, which ultimately stabilized FoxP3 expression and facilitated Treg cell differentiation. In NSCLC PDO models, pharmacological inhibition of glutamine metabolism reversed the immunosuppressive T cell phenotype and efficiently suppressed PDO growth. CONCLUSION: NSCLC CSCs mediate TME immunosuppression via a glutamine metabolism-dependent regulatory axis. Exosomal ROS-initiated FoxP3 post-translational modification is a novel mechanism underlying CSC-driven Treg differentiation. This study reveals an unreported immune evasion pathway in NSCLC and identifies glutamine metabolism as a viable therapeutic target for overcoming tumor immunosuppression.

papers.abstract_en: Uncommon epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant lung adenocarcinoma comprises clinically and biologically heterogeneous subgroups with variable sensitivity to targeted therapy. Incomplete responses and eventual progression suggest that factors beyond receptor inhibition influence disease persistence during therapy. This hypothesis-generating narrative review examines whether apoptosis repressor with caspase recruitment domain (ARC), encoded by nucleolar protein 3 (NOL3), warrants investigation as a downstream node in the regulation of apoptosis within an aging-informed framework. The available evidence is considered across three levels: direct evidence from uncommon EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma; evidence from broader EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma or lung cancer; and evidence extrapolated from other cancers or nonmalignant tissues. Within the literature evaluated, no primary study directly demonstrated mutation-specific ARC/NOL3 enrichment, induction after EGFR inhibition, functional dependence, or an association with post-treatment tumor cell survival or clinical outcomes in uncommon EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. Accordingly, established ARC functions in caspase regulation, mitochondrial protection, and stress tolerance are not interpreted as evidence of disease-specific causality. Instead, they provide a biological rationale for testing whether uncommon EGFR signaling, regulation of apoptosis, and aging-associated stress responses intersect in selected tumor contexts. We outline the experimental and clinical evidence required to evaluate this hypothesis, including mutation-specific expression analyses, functional perturbation studies, longitudinal sampling, and biomarker validation. The framework identifies experimental and clinical priorities for evaluating the potential role of ARC/NOL3 in this disease setting.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) represents the most prevalent type of lung cancer, accounting for 35‑40% of all lung cancer cases. Regulatory T cells (Tregs), a CD4+ T cell subtype with immunosuppressive functions, play a pivotal role in maintaining self‑tolerance under physiological conditions. Recent evidence has increasingly highlighted their involvement in various cancers. In LUAD, Treg infiltration into tissues undermines the immune anticancer response, correlating with disease stage, treatment efficacy and prognosis. By inhibiting robust anti‑tumor immune mechanisms, Tregs facilitate tumor immune escape in LUAD. Furthermore, elevated Treg cell accumulation in LUAD has been linked to reduced overall survival rates. Tregs serve as independent predictors for LUAD diagnosis in patients at high risk of recurrence. Systematic depletion of all Tregs to enhance anticancer efficacy poses risks of inducing severe autoimmune pathologies. Consequently, understanding the precise structure of tumor‑infiltrating Tregs is essential for effective targeting of these cells in tumors. Additionally, identifying candidate targets or methods for the specific elimination of tumor‑infiltrating Tregs is necessary for developing efficient and safe combination immunotherapy strategies for LUAD. The present study focuses on the regulatory role of Tregs in LUAD prognosis, immune escape and targeted therapies, elucidating the molecular mechanisms of Treg involvement and presenting associated therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. As a predominant immune cell population in the tumor microenvironment (TME), tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) play a critical role in tumor progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). TAMs can promote either antitumor immunity or immunosuppression depending on their polarization status. Iron regulatory protein 2 (IRP2) is a key regulator of intracellular iron homeostasis and has been reported to be upregulated in several tumor types. However, the role of IRP2 in the TME remains unclear. This study revealed the previously unrecognized role of IRP2 in NSCLC progression and explored its potential as a TAM-directed therapeutic target linked to programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) regulation. We found that IRP2 skewed TAMs toward an immunosuppressive state that promoted tumor cell proliferation and migration, and limited apoptosis. Furthermore, IRP2 may sustain PD-L1 expression in TAMs by limiting sphingosine kinase 1 (SphK1)-associated lysosomal degradation. In conclusion, our findings identify IRP2-dependent maintenance of the immunosuppressive TAM phenotype as a promising therapeutic target in NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) turnaround times (TAT) exceed two weeks and can delay the initiation of targeted therapy. Rapid cartridge-based platforms such as Idylla deliver single-gene or fusion results from minimal cytology material within hours, but time savings have not been systematically quantified. METHODS: Forty-two cases of non-small cell lung carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, melanoma, and mammary analogue secretory carcinoma of the salivary gland that underwent both Idylla testing (KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, and GeneFusion assays) and orthogonal NGS at a single academic center were reviewed. NGS TAT was calculated from specimen collection to report release, and Idylla results were modeled as available one day after collection. The primary outcome was per-case time savings (NGS TAT minus one day); treatment timelines were reconstructed from the medical record. Analyses were descriptive; no inferential testing was performed. A sensitivity analysis varied the modeled Idylla TAT from 1 to 3 days, and an adjusted estimate assigned no time saving to the two cartridge results that were not actionable on the day of collection. RESULTS: The median NGS TAT across all 42 cases was 20.0 days (IQR, 17.0-23.8; range, 8-51). Against the modeled 1-day Idylla TAT, the median time savings was 19.0 days per case (IQR, 16.0-22.8; range, 7-50), totaling 858 patient-days. Assigning no time saving to those two cases gave a median of 18.0 days and 817 patient-days. No patient received therapy that was subsequently contradicted by the sequencing result. In thirteen patients, the sequencing interval alone exceeded three weeks, and in seven, no systemic therapy was underway while the result was awaited. CONCLUSIONS: Same-day cartridge-based testing from cytology and small biopsy specimens could provide actionable results a median of 19 days earlier than standard NGS. Whether this translates into earlier treatment initiation was not assessed and requires prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: Lung and ovarian cancers account for substantial cancer morbidity and mortality worldwide. Plant-derived natural products represent promising alternatives in cancer therapy because of their structural diversity and ability to target multiple signaling pathways. Prosopis species are ethnomedicinal plants traditionally known for their antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities; however, their anticancer potential remains poorly explored. This study evaluates the anticancer properties of extracts of Prosopis cineraria, Prosopis farcta, and Prosopis juliflora, the Prosopis species growing in Qatar, against human lung (A549) and ovarian (SK-OV-3) cancer cells. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used to characterize their phytochemical composition. The cytotoxicity and anti-migratory activity of the three extracts were evaluated. Western blot analysis was performed to investigate the molecular effects of the extracts on proliferation- and apoptosis-related proteins. GC-MS profiling identified diverse low-molecular-weight bioactive compounds across the extracts, including several compounds detected only in P. juliflora, which exhibited the most potent cytotoxicity toward A549 and SK-OV-3 cells. All three extracts inhibited cancer cell migration, with P. juliflora showing the strongest effect. Furthermore, P. juliflora reduced the expression of proliferation and survival markers and increased the expression of pro-apoptotic proteins. These findings identify P. juliflora as the most active of the three tested Prosopis extracts and support further investigation of its in vitro anticancer potential.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pleural involvement is an important but poorly described manifestation of feline pulmonary carcinoma. Thoracic ultrasonography may identify pleural abnormalities and accessible targets for cytologic sampling in cats with pleural effusion. OBJECTIVES: To describe ultrasonographic features of pleural thickening in cats with pulmonary carcinoma and pleural effusion and summarise cytologic findings from pleural effusion and ultrasound-guided lesion sampling. METHODS: Medical records from one referral hospital were retrospectively reviewed for cats with pulmonary carcinoma or metastatic epithelial neoplasia consistent with pulmonary origin, pleural effusion, and stored thoracic ultrasound images. Images were reviewed in consensus by three observers for distribution, location, shape, maximal thickness, echogenicity, homogeneity, and suspected intercostal muscle invasion. RESULTS: Twenty-two cats were included. Pleural thickening was recorded in all cats. Thickening was classified as diffuse in 12 cats, focal in 6, and multifocal in 4; however, scanning was not systematic across all thoracic regions. The representative or measured pleural abnormality was in the cranial pleural region in 18 cats. Maximal pleural thickness was 5.6 ± 3.3 mm (median, 4.9 mm; range, 1.2-16.2 mm). Suspected intercostal muscle invasion was recorded in eight cats. Neoplastic cells were identified in pleural effusion cytology in 15/20 cats. Six cats underwent ultrasound-guided lesion sampling; cytologic or histopathologic findings were supportive of carcinoma in all 6, including 1 confirmed by biopsy. CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort, thoracic ultrasonography identified pleural thickening with variable morphology. Thickened pleura may represent a feasible sampling target, but prospective studies are needed to determine prevalence, distribution, sensitivity, and specificity.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Routine assessment of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and comprehensive next-generation sequencing (NGS) is recommended to guide treatment selection in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Obtaining adequate tissue for biomarker and molecular analyses is therefore essential. This study compared sample adequacy for PD-L1 and NGS testing between shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) and computed tomography-guided transthoracic lung biopsy (CTTB) in patients with NSCLC. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of patients with NSCLC who underwent biopsy of PPL by ssRAB or CTTB between June 2020 and December 2025. Demographic, procedural, pathological, biomarker and molecular data were extracted from electronic medical records, and descriptive statistics analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed. RESULTS: A total of 402 patients were included, comprising 198 in the ssRAB cohort and 204 in the CTTB cohort. ssRAB demonstrated significantly higher sample adequacy rates than CTTB for both PD-L1 (98.8% vs. 90.6%, p < 0.001) and NGS testing (92.3% vs. 79.1%, p = 0.005). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, ssRAB was independently associated with higher odds of PD-L1 sample adequacy (adjusted OR 11.48, 95% CI 2.89-78.30; p = 0.002) and NGS sample adequacy (adjusted OR 4.01, 95% CI 1.64-11.40; p = 0.004) compared with CTTB. In a separate model evaluating biopsy tools, cryobiopsy use was independently associated with higher odds of PD-L1 adequacy (adjusted OR 16.54, 95% CI 2.92-317.65; p = 0.010) and NGS adequacy (adjusted OR 5.83, 95% CI 1.93-25.39; p = 0.006) compared with non-cryobiopsy sampling. CONCLUSIONS: ssRAB-acquired specimens were associated with higher rates of PD-L1 and NGS sample adequacy than CTTB-acquired specimens in patients with NSCLC. Future prospective studies are needed to better understand the procedural and specimen-related factors underlying these differences.

papers.abstract_en: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially fatal immune-related adverse event of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung cancer, and many machine-learning (ML), computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep-learning, and clinical models have been proposed to predict it. This systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and SinoMed, supplemented by citation searching and other sources, with independent dual-reviewer screening throughout and a reproducible PubMed verification search updated to August 16, 2026. Twelve peer-reviewed lung-cancer CIP-occurrence models (4,875 patients, 1,057 events) formed the main analysis; validation C-statistics were pooled on the logit scale with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp intervals, stratified by validation design. The pooled validation C-statistic was 0.82 (95% confidence interval 0.75-0.88) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 90.7%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 0.51-0.95, which is the decision-relevant quantity. By validation design, internal cross-validation pooled to 0.83, internal split-sample to 0.76, and only two studies reported external validation (0.84 and 0.92, described narratively). Imaging-based models (k = 8) showed numerically higher discrimination than clinical models (k = 4; 0.85 versus 0.78, moderator p = 0.46) without a statistically significant difference, and this comparison is confounded by design covariates. Estimates were stable on leave-one-out, alternative-model, cohort-overlap, and standard-error-source sensitivity analyses (range 0.80-0.84). Under the standard Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool, applied independently by two reviewers with consensus resolution, two studies were at high, nine at unclear, and one at low overall risk of bias; certainty of evidence was low (very low under a stricter appraisal scenario, which left the pooled estimate essentially unchanged). Current models separate risk groups on average but remain unready for clinical use; adequately powered, externally validated, and calibration-reported models are needed.

papers.abstract_en: To evaluate the clinical utility of combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation analysis in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) for lung cancer diagnosis using methylation-specific PCR (MSP). The study aimed to combine BALF methylation results with bronchoscopic cytology, serum tumor markers, and imaging data to assess their diagnostic value. A total of 77 patients were recruited and divided into two groups: 57 patients with lung cancer and 20 control subjects. The methylation levels of SHOX2 and RASSF1A in BALF samples were analyzed using MSP. General data, serum markers, imaging, cytology, and pathology results were collected. The methylation levels were compared between the two groups, and differences in methylation levels across different pathological types and stages were analyzed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to determine the cutoff values. The diagnostic performance of combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation testing was compared with serum markers and cytology. The combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation test showed a sensitivity of 68.42% and a specificity of 95%, significantly improving the detection rate of lung adenocarcinoma. Higher methylation levels were observed in advanced-stage lung cancer compared with early-stage cases. The combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation test exhibited the highest sensitivity, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.817, compared with carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), cytokeratin 19 fragment 21-1 (CY211), and BALF cytology. The combined use of BALF cytology and methylation testing increased the detection rate to 73.68%, higher than BALF cytology alone (40.35%). The odds ratio for positive SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation in patients with bronchial cutoff signs was 15.167. Combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation testing can serve as an auxiliary diagnostic tool for lung cancer, outperforming serum markers and BALF cytology in diagnostic efficacy. Additionally, it can complement BALF cytology and provide a more accurate diagnosis. The presence of bronchial cutoff signs can be used as a relevant factor to predict positive SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation.

papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to investigate the interventional effects of Kaixin Powder(KXP) on the progression of lung adenocarcinoma(LUAD) under chronic stress and its underlying mechanism. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry(UPLC-MS/MS) was employed to characterize the chemical constituents of KXP, followed by network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses to screen for its potential targets. A chronic stress-associated lung cancer mouse model was established by axillary inoculation of Lewis lung carcinoma(LLC) cells combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress(CUMS). Sixty SPF-grade C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into the following groups: normal group, lung cancer group, model group, low-and high-dose KXP(13.65 and 27.3 g·kg~(-1)) groups, and fluoxetine(2 mg·kg~(-1)) group. Tumor growth indicators, including body weight, tumor mass, and tumor inhibition rate of mice were measured. Depression-like behaviors were observed by open field test(OFT) and sucrose preference test(SPT). Serum levels of stress factors such as corticosterone(Cort) and kynurenine(Kyn) were measured by ELISA. Histopathological changes in tumor tissue were assessed by hematoxylin-eosin(HE) staining. Peripheral blood T lymphocyte subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry. Intratumoral CD8~+T cells infiltration was detected by immunofluorescence, and the protein expression levels of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1(IDO1) and aryl hydrocarbon receptor(Ahr) were determined by Western blot. Serum ALT, AST, BUN, and Scr levels were measured to evaluate hepatic and renal safety. UPLC-MS/MS analysis characterized 157 chemical constituents of KXP. The protein expression levels of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1(IDO1) and aryl hydrocarbon receptor(Ahr) were detected by Western blot. In addition, serum ALT, AST, BUN, and Scr levels were measured to evaluate hepatic and renal safety. UPLC-MS identified 157 chemical constituents of KXP. Network pharmacology analysis obtained 367 potential targets, among which epidermal growth factor receptor(EGFR), protein kinase B alpha(AKT1), signal transducer and activator of transcription 3(STAT3), heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1(HSP90AA1), and IDO1 were screened as core targets. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes(KEGG) pathway analysis and molecular docking indicated that abnormal tryptophan metabolism mediated by IDO1 may be a potential mechanism underlying KXP intervention in LUAD complicated with depression. Animal experiments showed that, compared with the lung cancer group, the model group exhibited significantly accelerated tumor growth, increased structural disarray and atypia in HE-stained tumor tissue, obvious depression-like behaviors, and significantly elevated serum Cort and Kyn levels. In addition, the proportions of peripheral blood CD3~+ and CD3~+CD4~+T cells and the CD3~+CD4~+/CD3~+CD8~+ ratio significantly decreased, whereas the proportion of CD3~+CD8~+T cells significantly increased. Intratumoral CD8~+T cells infiltration was reduced, while the protein expression levels of IDO1 and Ahr were significantly upregulated. Compared with the model group, the high-dose KXP group showed significantly reduced tumor volume and tumor weight, with a tumor inhibition rate of 52.43%. KXP intervention improved depression-like behaviors to varying degrees, with the high-dose group showing more pronounced improvements in OFT activity indicators and SPT sucrose preference rate. Serum Cort and Kyn levels were significantly reduced in the high-dose KXP group. The proportions of peripheral blood CD3~+ and CD3~+CD4~+T cells and the CD3~+CD4~+/CD3~+CD8~+ ratio significantly increased in both low-and high-dose KXP groups. The low-dose KXP group showed significantly reduced IDO1 protein expression, while the high-dose group showed significantly reduced expression of both IDO1 and Ahr proteins. Safety evaluation showed that, within the experimental dose range, KXP had no obvious adverse effects on the morphology of major organs or on serum ALT, AST, BUN, and Scr levels. In conclusion, KXP ameliorates chronic stress and delays LUAD progression, and its mechanism may be associated with inhibition of the IDO1/Kyn/Ahr axis, correction of abnormal tryptophan metabolism, promotion of intratumoral CD8~+T cells infiltration, and improvement of the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.abstract_en: Radon is a globally recognized lung carcinogen and one of the main risk factors for lung cancer in nonsmokers. In Peru, recent evidence indicates elevated radon concentrations in homes in Metropolitan Lima and a possible contribution to the increase in lung cancer, especially in women, although national evidence primarily comes from ecological studies and is still insufficient to establish causality. Regulatory, technical, and surveillance gaps persist that hinder its control. This special article presents a narrative review of international and national evidence and aims to examine the current situation of radon exposure in Peru, identify the regulatory and surveillance gaps that limit its control, and propose specific mitigation measures aligned with international recommendations.

To ensure early detection, the German Social Accident Insurance (DGUV) offers lung cancer screening including a low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) for individuals with long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust and a smoking history of at least 30 pack years. However, evidence remains scarce about what encourages this group of people to participate in LDCT screening after medical consultation. METHODS: A secondary data analysis using routinely collected medical and administrative data between 2014 and 2024 was conducted in a cross-sectional design. This study aimed to investigate factors that could be used to predict the uptake of LDCT screening following a medical consultation. Exploratory logistic regression analysis was used to identify and assess possible predictors. RESULTS: The sample included n = 14,491 individuals (97% male; average age 67 years; average asbestos dust exposure 21 years; average cigarette consumption 43 pack years). 74% of individuals underwent LDCT screening after medical consultation. 13 predictors were included in the regression model. The model demonstrated a low level of variance explanation (Nagelkerkes R2 = 0.026). Younger individuals (OR: 0.96, p < 0.001), individuals with prolonged exposure to asbestos dust (OR: 1.01, p = 0.011) and with a history of pneumonia (OR: 1.16, p = 0.011) were more likely to undergo LDCT screening. CONCLUSION: The predictors showed only a low explanatory power. Further research should include non-participants and expand the exploratory model to include theoretically grounded predictors.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: First-line treatment options for HER2-altered advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain limited, especially in cases with HER2-EGFR co-alterations. While new agents like trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) have emerged, its real-world evidence in first line remains limited. METHODS: This study included patients with advanced NSCLC who had HER2 mutations or amplification and received first-line systemic therapy at six medical centers. Outcomes were evaluated following chemotherapy-based combinations, pan-HER tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), and T-DXd. Endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), one-year and two-year survival rates, and toxicity. RESULTS: A total of 69 patients were enrolled, comprising 45 with only HER2 alterations and 24 with HER2-EGFR co-alterations. In patients with only HER2-altered NSCLC, those receiving first-line T-DXd had an mPFS of 15.7 months (95% CI, 12.5-18.9), an ORR of 85.7%, and a DCR of 100.0%. The mPFS for patients receiving chemotherapy-based regimens, pan-HER TKIs, and chemotherapy plus pan-HER TKIs were 7.6 (95% CI, 6.6-8.5) months, 4.4 (95% CI, 4.0-4.9) months, and 7.0 (95% CI, 6.1-9.1) months, respectively. The ORR for the three groups above was 33.3%, 0, and 0, respectively. In subgroup analysis, patients with only HER2 alterations who did not harbor TP53 mutations had a longer PFS than those with TP53 co-mutations (8.7 m vs. 7.2 m; HR: 0.35; 95% CI: 0.11-0.99; P = 0.048). In patients with EGFR-HER2 co-alterations, first-line EGFR-TKI monotherapy yielded an mPFS of 9.7 (95% CI, 8.6-10.8) months, an ORR of 40.0%, and a DCR of 93.3%. Regarding safety, we did not observe Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs in first-line T-DXd treatment. CONCLUSIONS: First-line T-DXd showed promising activity signals in only HER2-altered NSCLC. In EGFR-HER2 co-altered patients, the EGFR-TKI monotherapy showed limited efficacy. The findings underscored the urgent need for prospective randomised trials.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, emphasizing the need for accurate, automated, and clinically interpretable diagnostic systems. Although existing deep learning (DL) models have achieved promising performance in classifying lung nodules as benign or malignant, most approaches are limited to binary classification and provide insufficient support for detailed tumor characterization and TNM staging. Furthermore, conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are effective in extracting local morphological features but often fail to capture long-range spatial dependencies. In contrast, transformer-based models can learn global contextual information but may compromise fine-grained local feature representation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid ResNet-50-Vision Transformer with Radiomic Feature Fusion (ReViT-RF) framework for lung tumor classification and component-wise TNM stage prediction using thoracic computed tomography (CT) images from the publicly available Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) dataset. The primary clinical objectives of the proposed framework are to: (i) classify pulmonary nodules as benign or malignant, and (ii) predict individual TNM components, including primary tumor extent (T), lymph node involvement (N), and metastatic status (M) for malignant cases. To improve tumor visibility and image quality, CT images are initially preprocessed using Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and intensity normalization. The proposed ReViT-RF architecture integrates the complementary advantages of ResNet-50 and Vision Transformer (ViT) for comprehensive feature learning. The CNN branch extracts local morphological, textural, and structural characteristics, whereas the transformer branch captures long-range spatial relationships and global contextual dependencies. In addition, handcrafted radiomic features, including shape, size, texture, and spatial descriptors, are fused with deep features to provide clinically meaningful information for accurate TNM component prediction. The dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio, with data augmentation applied only to the training set to prevent information leakage. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 97.62% for benign-malignant classification, along with high precision, recall, and F1-score values. Moreover, independent prediction of TNM components provides detailed stage-related information rather than relying on a single aggregated stage label, enabling more precise tumor assessment and clinical decision support. Furthermore, explainability analysis using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) identifies the critical tumor regions contributing to model predictions, improving interpretability and enhancing clinician confidence. Overall, by combining hybrid deep feature extraction, radiomic feature fusion, component-wise TNM stage prediction, and explainable AI analysis, the proposed ReViT-RF framework provides a reliable, comprehensive, and clinically interpretable solution for automated lung tumor analysis.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma exhibits diverse pathological features, some of which for example, histological grading and tumor spread through air spaces (STAS), can be used for prognosis. Extra-alveolar invasion (EX) is a unique pathological factor focused on depth of invasion, and is defined as tumor infiltration into periarterial, peribronchiolar, or interlobular septal stroma. We recently suggested EX as a prognostic indicator, but its significance in sublobar resection remains unclear. We investigated the prognostic impact of EX in 116 patients with pT1mi-pT2a non-mucinous lung adenocarcinoma treated by segmentectomy or wedge resection. EX was evaluated using elastic fiber staining. Among 10 recurrent cases, 8 were EX-positive, and 2 were EX-negative and STAS-positive. The EX(-)/STAS(+) cases had local recurrence, while the EX(+) cases exhibited metastatic recurrence. The pT1abc EX(+) group showed significantly shorter recurrence-free survival (RFS) than the pT1abc EX(-) group, but no significant differences were observed when compared with the pT2 group. EX(+ )/STAS(-) and EX(+ )/STAS(+) groups showed significantly shorter RFS than EX(-)/STAS(-) group, but EX(-)/STAS(+) group did not. In conclusion, EX was associated with poor prognosis after sublobar resection of lung adenocarcinoma. Combined evaluation of EX and STAS may improve postoperative risk stratification.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma is the most prevalent subtype of non-small cell lung cancer and exhibits a high tendency for distant metastasis. However, uterine metastasis with synchronous multiorgan involvement is extremely rare and prone to misdiagnosis due to atypical clinical presentations. To date, fewer than 20 cases of lung adenocarcinoma metastasizing to the uterus have been documented globally, most of which present with typical gynecological symptoms, making our atypical case highly educational and complementary to existing clinical data. CASE: Herein, we describe a 77-year-old postmenopausal female patient who initially presented with lumbago and dizziness without typical pulmonary or gynecological symptoms, with an ECOG performance status of 1. Imaging studies raised suspicion of a primary uterine malignancy, but pathological biopsy, immunohistochemistry, and genomic testing ultimately confirmed advanced lung adenocarcinoma with multiorgan metastases (uterus, lung, liver, bone). Molecular analysis identified an EGFR exon 21 p.L858R mutation, and the patient received palliative local radiotherapy combined with osimertinib targeted therapy. During treatment, the patient developed mild radiation-induced fatigue and slight myelosuppression, which were fully relieved after symptomatic supportive care, with no severe unexpected adverse events observed. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates the atypical metastatic pattern of lung adenocarcinoma, underscores the pivotal role of pathological and immunohistochemical examinations in differentiating primary from metastatic tumors, and offers a reference for managing diagnostically challenging cases. Early and accurate diagnosis coupled with genomic-guided personalized therapy is critical for enhancing quality of life and prognosis in patients with advanced lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: In recent years, pulmonary segmentectomy has become a preferred treatment option for early-stage lung cancer. The primary factor encouraging clinicians to choose segmentectomy is the assumption of greater parenchymal preservation. In this study, we investigated the parenchyma-sparing effect of robotic pulmonary segmentectomy compared with robotic lobectomy using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted 3-dimensional (3D) volumetric analysis. METHODS: Preoperative and postoperative thoracic computed tomography scans of patients diagnosed with lung cancer between January 2022 and December 2025 who underwent robotic lobectomy or segmentectomy were analyzed using Synapse 3D software. Resected, remaining, expected, and measured lung volumes were calculated. Differences between predicted and measured values were analyzed using the independent-samples t test or the Mann-Whitney U test, depending on the data distribution. RESULTS: A total of 39 patients were included in the study. Lobectomy was performed in 21 patients, and segmentectomy in 18. The median resected lung volume was 360.5 mL (interquartile range [IQR]: 198-550) in the segmentectomy group and 896 mL (IQR: 599-1194) in the lobectomy group (P < .001). The difference in expected remaining lung volume percentages between the lobectomy and segmentectomy groups was statistically significant (P < .001), whereas the difference in measured postoperative remaining lung volumes was not statistically significant (P = .1). CONCLUSION: This pilot study demonstrated that robotic segmentectomy may not provide the expected parenchymal preservation advantage compared with lobectomy. Further prospective multicenter studies with larger cohorts are required.

papers.abstract_en: Earlier tissue-based studies report heterogeneous CYP and GST protein expression in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but simultaneous assessment of phase I and II enzymes in paired tumour and peripheral normal tissues remains limited and their expression patterns poorly characterised across the two major NSCLC histological subtypes, namely adenocarcinoma (AC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Cytoplasmic staining intensity was scored from 0 to 3. Tissue and subtype comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test, and associations with clinical variables were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. CYP2E1 expression was significantly higher in tumour than in normal tissue in the combined NSCLC group and in both histological subtypes (p<0.05). CYP1A1 expression was higher in AC tumours than in normal tissue and SCC tumours (both p<0.05). GSTM1 expression was higher in tumour tissue in the combined NSCLC group and in the SCC subgroup and was also higher in SCC than in AC tumours (p<0.05). GSTT1 expression was higher in AC than SCC tumours (p<0.05). CYP1B1 and GSTP1 were highly expressed in both tissue compartments but showed no significant tumour-specific increase. CYP and GST isoenzymes therefore showed tissue- and subtype-dependent rather than uniform expression patterns in NSCLC. The differences observed in CYP2E1, CYP1A1, GSTM1, and GSTT1 suggest that AC and SCC may differ in xenobiotic metabolism and cellular defence, and that these isoenzymes may contribute to metabolic processes associated with NSCLC pathogenesis.

papers.abstract_en: Exosomes derived from lung cancer cells play a critical role in modulating the tumour microenvironment, particularly through their effects on macrophage polarization. We investigated how exosomes from A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells, both unstimulated and stimulated with a toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) agonist, influence the phenotype and function of THP-1 derived macrophages. We used differential centrifugation and immunobead assay to isolate exosomes. Exosomes from unstimulated A549 cells promoted a mixed M1/M2 macrophage phenotype with a bias towards M2 polarization, while exosomes from TLR4-stimulated A549 cells reduced M2 marker expression without affecting M1 polarization. Both types of exosomes increased macrophage phagocytic capacity compared to PMA-differentiated controls, but TLR4-agonists did not increase it further. These findings provide new insights into how TLR agonist-stimulated lung cancer-derived exosomes shape macrophage phenotypes and functions, with implications for understanding tumour-immune interactions and developing novel therapeutic strategies targeting the tumour microenvironment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cigarette smoke contains numerous toxic compounds that can induce oxidative stress and DNA damage. While smoking is a well-established driver of lung cancer initiation, the biological consequences of continued exposure after tumor establishment remain poorly understood. This study investigated the genomic and phenotypic effects of chronic cigarette smoke exposure in established lung cancer cells. METHODS: Human lung adenocarcinoma A549 cells were chronically exposed to cigarette smoke extract to model sustained exposure. Cellular proliferation and migration assays were performed to evaluate phenotypic changes. Transcriptomic profiling was used to examine alterations in gene expression related to cell cycle regulation and DNA repair pathways. Whole-genome sequencing was conducted to identify mutational signatures associated with genomic instability. Tumor growth and histological features were further evaluated using xenograft models. RESULTS: Chronic cigarette smoke extract exposure increased the clonogenic capacity and migratory behavior of A549 cells and induced phenotypic features consistent with partial epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Transcriptomic analysis revealed disruption of cell cycle regulation and reduced expression of homologous recombination DNA repair genes, including RAD51. Whole-genome sequencing identified mutational signatures associated with oxidative damage, mismatch repair deficiency, and homologous recombination defects. These alterations were accompanied by increased tumor growth and cellular atypia in xenograft models. CONCLUSIONS: Chronic cigarette smoke exposure may enhance genomic instability and promote aggressive phenotypes in established lung cancer cells, suggesting that continued smoking after cancer development may contribute to tumor progression.

papers.abstract_en: Mediastinal nodal classification in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) at the N0/N1-N2/N3 treatment-defining boundary guides therapeutic strategy and is commonly finalized in multidisciplinary tumor board (MDT) meetings. We compared positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) and endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) against MDT assignment and quantified discordance at this threshold. We retrospectively analyzed 114 consecutive NSCLC patients who underwent both PET/CT and EBUS-TBNA before MDT review. Nodal stage was dichotomized as N0/N1 vs N2/N3. Because the MDT decision incorporates both modalities, agreement with MDT is reported as observed agreement and Cohen κ together with the direction of discordance, rather than as sensitivity and specificity. In the subgroup with surgical mediastinal staging, both modalities and the MDT category were compared with histopathology. MDT assigned N2/N3 in 84 patients (73.7%). Relative to the MDT category, PET/CT over-classified 16 patients (14.0%) and under-classified 9 (7.9%). EBUS-TBNA under-classified 15 of the 43 patients it classified N0/N1 (34.9%), and under-classification persisted among the 25 patients in whom every sampled station was diagnostic (8/25, 32.0%); 12 of these 15 assignments rested on clinical-radiological course rather than histopathology. Agreement with the MDT category was 85.1% (κ = 0.662) for EBUS-TBNA and 78.1% (κ = 0.389) for PET/CT; because malignant cytology was definitional for the MDT category, 67 of 97 concordant EBUS-TBNA classifications (69.1%) were determined by that rule and do not measure EBUS-TBNA performance. Against surgical histopathology in 18 patients, PET/CT classified 11 of 13 pathologically N0 patients as N2/N3 (specificity 15.4%; 95% CI, 4.3-42.2) and EBUS-TBNA identified 2 of 5 with pathological N2 disease (sensitivity 40.0%; 95% CI, 11.8-76.9). At the treatment-defining nodal boundary, the two modalities diverged from the multidisciplinary decision in opposite directions: PET/CT over-classified nodal status, whereas EBUS-TBNA under-classified in approximately 1 in 3 patients it had assigned N0/N1, including those in whom sampling was complete, although most of these assignments rested on clinical course rather than tissue. These findings are consistent with guideline recommendations that PET-positive mediastinal nodes require tissue confirmation and that a negative endosonographic result be interpreted alongside pretest probability and station coverage.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary papillary adenoma is currently considered a benign tumor; however, a few cases have been reported in the past with potential for malignancy. Therefore, the histological nature of papillary adenomas remains controversial. This article presents a rare case of a multifocal papillary adenoma with uncertain malignant potential, featuring an ERBIN-BRAF gene fusion and an APC mutation, along with a literature review, to enhance understanding of this tumor. CASE DESCRIPTION: The patient sought medical consultation due to symptoms of cough and sputum production. Imaging showed a high-density, lobulated nodule in the posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe, surrounded by multiple smaller nodules. Postpulmonary lobectomy, histopathological examination revealed a large nodule composed of a single papillary structure, with the papillary surface covered by a single layer of cuboidal or low-columnar epithelium. Local areas showed transition to surrounding alveolar epithelium, and well-formed glands were observed in the proliferative fibrous tissue, with local stromal fibrosis. Some tumor cells in the surrounding small nodules grew in a lepidic fashion, with cellular morphology similar to that of the large nodule. Immunohistochemical staining showed that tumor cells were positive for TTF-1, CK, CK7, and Napsin A, with a few cells expressing P53 and a Ki-67 index of approximately 8%. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) identified an APC gene mutation (Exon 16, p.E1306∗) and an ERBIN exon3-BRAF exon11 fusion. Given that BRAF alterations have been implicated in lung carcinogenesis, a similar BRAF-mediated tumorigenic pathway may be active in this tumor; therefore, complete resection of the adenoma may be indicated. The tumor's multifocal distribution and molecular alterations suggest that this case represents a papillary adenoma with uncertain malignant potential. CONCLUSIONS: Currently, there is no established standard treatment for such tumors, and the tumor in this case underwent pulmonary lobectomy. Future studies should accumulate more cases to clarify the prognosis and treatment guidelines for this type of tumor.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Several therapeutic targets for non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) rely on protein expression by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Most biomarkers are validated on formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue; however, cytologic specimens, including cell blocks (CBs), that are subject to preanalytical variables are increasingly used. The objective of this study was to evaluate predictive IHC biomarkers in NSCLC CBs and compare them with surgical pathology (SP) specimens. METHODS: The authors retrospectively reviewed NSCLC cytology specimens that underwent predictive IHC testing for hepatocyte growth factor receptor (c-MET), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), and programmed death-ligand-1 (PD-L1) between January 2019 and June 2025. IHC was performed on CBs that were centrifuged with equal amounts of ethanol and formalin before FFPE processing. Equal numbers of NSCLC SP specimens with available biomarker testing were included for comparison. Predictive IHC scores that were considered therapy-eligible were c-MET IHC 3+, HER2 IHC 3+, and PD-L1-positive tumor proportion scores. Statistical analyses were performed using the Fisher exact test, with p < .05 considered significant. RESULTS: The cohort included 414 cases (cytology specimens, N = 212; SP specimens, N = 212 [60% biopsy, 40% resection]). Cytology specimens demonstrated a significantly higher proportion of strong 3+ c-MET expression (40%) compared with SP specimens (10%; p < .0001). Similarly, high PD-L1 expression was more frequent in cytology specimens (32% vs. 20%; p = .0079). HER2 expression was similar between groups, with no significant difference in HER2 IHC 3+ rates (p = .34). CONCLUSIONS: Predictive IHC testing is performed on NSCLC cytology to identify patients for therapeutic targets. papers.abstract_en: Acquired resistance to epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-targeted therapy remains a major obstacle in the treatment of EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study investigated whether repurposing mebendazole (MBZ), a microtubule-disrupting agent, could restore sensitivity to gefitinib in gefitinib-resistant HCC827 GR5 cells. Gefitinib monotherapy showed minimal cytotoxicity, reducing cell viability only marginally (92.7 ± 1.5%), whereas MBZ significantly decreased viability to 79.7 ± 0.6% at 0.1 µM and 29.7 ± 0.6% at 0.5 µM (p < 0.001). Combination treatment (gefitinib 1 µM + MBZ 0.1 µM) further reduced viability to 37.7 ± 0.6% (p < 0.001). Mechanistically, alkaline comet assay revealed significantly increased single-strand DNA damage in the combination group (tail intensity 22.33 ± 0.56%, p < 0.001), while neutral comet assay confirmed elevated double-strand DNA breaks. MBZ also induced dose-dependent γ-H2AX activation (p < 0.001), supporting replication stress-associated DNA damage signaling. In vivo, combination therapy significantly suppressed tumor growth, prolonging tumor doubling time from 6.2 days in controls to 25 days and increasing growth delay to 18.8 days (p < 0.01), without substantial systemic toxicity. Collectively, these findings identify replication stress vulnerability as a therapeutically exploitable axis and support MBZ repurposing as an adjuvant strategy to overcome gefitinib resistance.

papers.abstract_en: In real-world clinical settings, patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) display significant heterogeneity, highlighting the need to identify key prognostic biomarkers and clinical factors. This retrospective study included 340 advanced NSCLC patients treated with ICIs. Cox regression analyses identified factors associated with progression-free survival (PFS). A Nutritional Inflammatory Hematological Risk Index (NIHRI) was constructed using these factors, and a prognostic nomogram was developed. Performance was assessed using the C-index, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA), with internal validation via bootstrapping. Hemoglobin and the albumin-to-alkaline phosphatase ratio (AAPR) were independent prognostic factors. The NIHRI, combining dichotomized hemoglobin (< 120 g/L vs. ≥120 g/L) and AAPR (< 0.56 vs. ≥0.56), stratified patients into low- (0 points), intermediate- (1 point), and high-risk (2 points) groups, with significantly different PFS (P<0.001). The nomogram, incorporating NIHRI, tumor stage, PD-L1, and ECOG-PS, demonstrated a C-index of 0.70 (optimism-corrected: 0.69) and predictive accuracy for 1-, 2-, and 3-year PFS (AUCs: 0.81, 0.85, and 0.88, respectively). DCA confirmed its acceptable clinical net benefit. We developed and validated a novel prognostic tool, the NIHRI, based on a combination of hemoglobin and AAPR. This integrated nomogram provides a non-invasive and clinically accessible quantitative method for predicting prognosis in patients with NSCLC undergoing immunotherapy, thereby aiding in personalized clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: An intraoperative ACTH monitoring during resection of hormone-secreting neuroendocrine neoplasms remains a subject of a debate. We present the case of a 36-year-old man with clinical and biochemical features of ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism. Dynamic endocrine testing, including the high-dose dexamethasone suppression test, metyrapone test, and desmopressin stimulation test resulted in inconclusive results, precluding clear differentiation between Cushing's disease and ectopic Cushing's syndrome. Pituitary imaging revealed no definite focal lesion, whereas chest imaging detected a small pulmonary nodule along with an incidental adrenal adenoma. Taking into account rapid clinical course and the severity of clinical symptoms surgical resection of the lung lesion was undertaken with intraoperative ACTH monitoring. Due to compilation of factors patient was sent to thoracic surgery without delay. A transient ACTH surge was observed during first stage tumor excision and, even though intraoperative pathological and surgical findings indicated the complete tumor resection, which contributed to the decision to extend the procedure to an upper lobectomy, after which a marked and sustained decline in ACTH concentrations was observed. Histopathological examination confirmed a typical pulmonary carcinoid tumor, and surgical treatment resulted in clinical and biochemical remission, followed by gradual recovery of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. This case highlights the limitations of dynamic testing and imaging in ECS, particularly in indolent presentation, and underscored the potential value of intraoperative ACTH monitoring as an adjunctive tool for tumor localization and surgical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Average intensity projection (AIP) is an image generation method obtained by averaging the images of each phase of 4D-CT. This study aimed to evaluate tumor respiratory motion and, using the union of contours from all 4D-CT phases (4DTotal) as the reference, to compare contour agreement among contours derived from 3D-CT, maximum intensity projection (MIP), and AIP images. In addition, dose metrics in treatment planning were evaluated to explore the dosimetric impact of contour differences among the image sets. METHODS: Eight patients who underwent lung stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) at our institution were included. Tumor motion was first characterized from centroid positions across ten 4D-CT phases. Next, 4DTotal was generated by taking the union of the contours extracted from each phase. Finally, contours from 4D-CT AIP, 4D-CT MIP, and slow-scan 3D-CT (3DSlow) were compared with 4DTotal using volume difference, centroid difference, Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Jaccard index, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), mean surface distance (MSD), and surface Dice similarity coefficient with a 2-mm tolerance. In addition, treatment plans were generated using each contour set, and Dmax (cGy), lung V5 (%), lung V20 (%), conformity index (CI), and homogeneity index (HI) were compared. RESULTS: Tumor motion was greatest in the inferior-superior direction and was generally multi-directional. For AIP, centroid difference was ≤1 mm in each direction (LR/AP/IS), and the median values of DSC, Jaccard index, HD95, MSD, and surface DSC (2 mm) were 0.831, 0.711, 1.707 mm, 0.451 mm, and 0.981, respectively, showing good geometric agreement with 4DTotal. No significant differences were observed between AIP and MIP, whereas both AIP and MIP showed better agreement than 3DSlow. In the dose evaluation, no significant overall differences were observed for any metric among the four contour sets. In the exploratory analysis, paired comparisons using 4DTotal as the reference showed a directional decrease in lung V20 for AIP and a directional increase in CI for MIP. These findings should not be interpreted as definitive conclusions, but rather as results of an exploratory analysis based on a limited number of cases. CONCLUSION: The AIP method showed good geometric approximation to 4DTotal and may represent the time-dependent displacement of tumor position within a single dataset. In this limited exploratory analysis, no major disadvantage in treatment planning was observed. However, the observed changes in dose metrics, including lung V20, should not be interpreted as evidence of dosimetric superiority and require further validation. Because of uncertainty in the reference contour and the limited number of cases, further investigation is needed to clarify its clinical significance.
