papers.abstract_en: Metastasis remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, a process in which circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central but incompletely understood role. Although most CTCs are rapidly eliminated during circulation through detachment-induced anoikis and fluid shear stress (SS)-triggered apoptosis, a subset of CTCs can survive these hostile conditions; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. To investigate this, we developed a microfluidic circulatory system that mimics physiological SS and performed transcriptomic profiling of A549 lung cancer cells under SS, attached, and static suspension conditions. Through this approach, we identified the ROS-CD44-Ezrin axis as a potential mechanosignaling module that may contribute to CTC survival under shear stress. In this cascade, SS-induced ROS and CD44 converge to activate Ezrin via phosphorylation at Thr567. Once activated, Ezrin appears to coordinate its two canonical functions-membrane-cytoskeleton reinforcement and pro-survival signaling via PI3K/AKT/Bcl-2 and NF-κB/p38/JNK pathways-within this specific mechanobiological context to preserve cell integrity and limit apoptosis. Our findings suggest that these well-established molecular functions are differentially engaged under shear stress, revealing a context-dependent survival mechanism that may offer opportunities for therapeutic exploration, pending further validation in more clinically relevant models.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The malignant progression of nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is closely related to cancer stemness. Histone deacetylase 4 (HDAC4) plays a regulatory role in lung cancer, but its effect on NSCLC stemness remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role and mechanism of HDAC4 in NSCLC stemness. METHODS: In this study, a tumor-bearing model was established by subcutaneously injecting A549 cells into the right dorsal side of nude mice. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry were used to measure gene and protein expression levels. Flow cytometry, sphere formation assays, and Transwell experiments were employed to assess cancer cell stemness, migration, and invasion. Additionally, a kit was used to measure changes in glutamine metabolism-related indicators. RESULTS: In this study, we found that knocking down HDAC4 expression inhibited the expression of SRY-box transcription factor 2 (SOX2), octamer-binding transcription factor 4 (OCT4), and nanog homeobox (NANOG) in A549 cells; it also reduced the proportions of CD133- and CD44-positive cells and suppressed their sphere formation, cell migration, and invasion abilities. Furthermore, HDAC4 knockdown inhibited glutamine uptake, glutamate production, α-ketoglutarate levels, and glutaminase (GLS) activity. Notably, treatment with the additional glutamine metabolism inhibitor CB-839 attenuated the promoting effects of HDAC4 overexpression on the stemness, migration, and invasion of A549 cells. In addition, HDAC4 promoted the expression of hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α) and solute carrier family 38 member 2 (SLC38A2); after overexpressing HIF-1α, the inhibitory effect of HDAC4 knockdown on SLC38A2 expression in A549 cells was weakened. CONCLUSION: Our study reveals a critical mechanism by which HDAC4 enhances glutamine metabolism through upregulation of HIF-1α expression to promote SLC38A2 expression, thereby driving NSCLC stemness and progression.

papers.abstract_en: Drug therapies targeting vasculature in metastatic cancer have not been highly effective and are therefore currently limited to an adjunctive role, such as in combination regimens. The development of novel, more effective therapeutic strategies with new mechanisms of action is therefore greatly needed. In a previous study, we reported a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based vascular-disrupting strategy utilizing cyclic RGD peptide-modified LNPs encapsulating small interfering RNA against Fas ligand (cRGD-LNP/siFasL). We combined this strategy for selective targeting of tumor endothelial cells with stimulator of interferon genes (STING) agonist-loaded LNPs (STING-LNPs). Here, we have demonstrated the potential of such combination therapy in treating lung metastases. We found that cRGD-LNPs accumulated in the vasculature within tumor colonies in the lung. A combination of cRGD-LNP/siFasL and STING-LNP induced significant antitumor effects in mouse models of Renca and 4T1 lung metastases. Moreover, this combination therapy reduced the vasculature within tumor colonies, with no obvious change in the surrounding normal lung tissue, indicating preferential vascular disruption. These findings demonstrate that the combination therapy exerts antitumor activity against lung metastases through tumor vascular disruption, indicating that such treatment is potentially a potent disrupter of the vascularity in metastatic tumors.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVE: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are essential in the modulation of cellular activities. Studies suggest that miR-3615 may possess a tumour-suppressive function in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD); however, its precise role and molecular mechanisms in LUAD progression remain incompletely understood. The aim of the study is to systematically investigate the biological functions and underlying mechanisms of miR-3615 in LUAD. MATERIAL AND METHODS: The expression of miR-3615 in LUAD cell lines was quantified by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Subsequently, its functional effects on proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis were evaluated in A549 and H1299 cells using the CCK-8 assay, Transwell assay, and flow cytometry, respectively. Potential target genes of miR-3615 were predicted and functionally annotated using bioinformatics methods. The binding interaction of miR-3615 with the CALML4 gene was demonstrated via a dual-luciferase reporter assay. RESULTS: miR-3615 expression was notably downregulated in LUAD cell lines compared with normal cells. Overexpression of miR-3615 inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion capabilities of LUAD cells while promoting apoptosis. Integrated bioinformatics analysis involving target prediction and functional enrichment identified CALML4 as a key candidate target gene of miR-3615. CALML4 was confirmed as a direct target of miR-3615. The effects of miR-3615 mimic on LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis were partly attenuated by CALML4 overexpression. CONCLUSIONS: miR-3615 exerts its functional impact on LUAD cells by directly downregulating CALML4, thereby curbing proliferation, migration, and invasion and promoting apoptosis. The elucidated miR-3615/CALML4 axis advances the theoretical foundation for studying LUAD development.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionised the management of advanced malignancies, but can cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including vision-threatening complications such as optic neuropathy. Ocular irAEs have been described with several programmed death-1/programmed death-ligand 1 and cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 inhibitors, but ocular toxicities of tislelizumab have so far been limited to Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada (VKH)-like uveitis, panuveitis and retinal vasculitis. We describe a woman with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma who was treated with second-line gemcitabine, carboplatin and tislelizumab. After the second cycle of chemo-immunotherapy, she developed painless, progressive bilateral visual blurring in the absence of intracranial disease. Ophthalmic assessment was consistent with toxic optic neuropathy in the context of ongoing tislelizumab exposure, and other causes were excluded. Tislelizumab was discontinued and high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g/day for 5 days) was administered, without ICI re-challenge. Visual function did not improve, indicating an irreversible optic nerve injury. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of toxic optic neuropathy associated with tislelizumab, extending the spectrum of tislelizumab-related ocular irAEs beyond previously documented VKH-like panuveitis, VKH-like uveitis and retinal vasculitis. This case highlights the importance of early recognition of visual symptoms and periodic ophthalmic assessment in patients receiving ICIs, as well as decision-making regarding ICI continuation or discontinuation when sight-threatening neuro-ophthalmic irAEs are suspected.

papers.abstract_en: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis. Given the association between mitochondrial dysregulation and LUSC, the aim of the present study was to identify mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt)‑related candidate genes associated with LUSC and to explore their potential functional relevance. In the present study, differential expression, univariate Cox and survival analyses were combined to identify a UPRmt‑associated key gene in LUSC. Gene set enrichment analysis was then performed, and overexpression (OE) and knockdown cell lines were used to clarify its function using western blotting, Cell Counting Kit‑8, colony formation and Transwell® invasion assays. Using bioinformatics tools and a review of the literature, PTEN‑induced kinase 1 (PINK1) was singled out as a key gene in LUSC samples. Elevated PINK1 expression was associated with worse survival outcomes. A total of 117 pathways were enriched by PINK1, with the top 5 including 'focal adhesion' and 'mitogen‑activated protein kinase signaling pathway'. Using experimental analysis, it was observed that PINK1 significantly enhanced the proliferative, migratory, invasive and colony forming abilities of tumor cells, thereby exacerbating LUSC. Furthermore, these enhancements were diminished by the application of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) inhibitor. It was also noted that the expression levels of protein kinase B (AKT), p‑AKT, Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) and vinculin were all elevated in OE‑PINK1 cells. Collectively, these findings indicated that PINK1 exerted its influence on LUSC through the FAK/AKT/RhoA/vinculin pathway. The present study identified PINK1 as a key gene in LUSC, exerting its influence through the FAK/AKT/RhoA/vinculin pathway, thereby presenting a potential novel therapeutic target for the treatment of LUSC in the future.

papers.abstract_en: Burkholderia pseudomallei, the causative agent of melioidosis, is a gram-negative bacterium historically endemic to Southeast Asia and Northern Australia. However, recent environmental detection along the Gulf Coast and an increasing number of reported cases in non-travelers have raised questions regarding potential endemicity and environmental establishment in the Southern United States. We report a case of putatively locally acquired pulmonary melioidosis in a Florida resident with no recent international travel history, illustrating the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges posed by this rare pathogen. The patient presented with fever, pleuritic chest pain, and hypoxia following a period of severe weather. Computed tomography (CT) of the chest revealed multiple solid pulmonary nodules with ground-glass opacities and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Given his underlying stage 3b chronic kidney disease (CKD), the patient was treated with an intensive course of intravenous ceftazidime followed by oral doxycycline monotherapy, achieving full clinical recovery. Follow-up imaging at 3 months demonstrated complete resolution of the pulmonary nodules. This case emphasizes the importance of considering melioidosis in the differential diagnosis for non-resolving community-acquired pneumonia or significant pulmonary nodules in the Southern United States, even in the absence of international travel. Risk factors such as diabetes mellitus and severe weather events are key clinical clues. While trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole remains the preferred eradication therapy, doxycycline may serve as a potential alternative for patients with renal impairment when first-line therapy is contraindicated.

papers.authors: Mahdi ZA, AlmjalawI BSA, Naimuzzaman M, Hasan MM, Kumer A, Al-Alaq FT, Al-Dahmoshi HOM, Rahman F et al.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches. This study employed an integrated computational pipeline to evaluate 14 phytochemicals from R. mucronata. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G* level were performed to characterize electronic properties of the ligands. Molecular docking studies were conducted using both AutoDock Vina (PyRx) and Schrödinger Glide against the Keap1 Kelch domain (PDB 1X2J) and the YEATS2 YEATS domain (PDB 5XNV). Top-ranked complexes were subjected to 100-ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in Desmond, and pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles were predicted using SwissADME and pkCSM. Among the screened compounds, ligand L10 (cyclohexane-1,2,3,4,5,6-hexaol) exhibited the smallest HOMO-LUMO energy gap (0.36 eV), favorable binding affinities (Glide score of -7.789 kcal/mol against 1X2J), multiple hydrogen-bonding interactions, and stable complex behavior during MD simulations (Cα RMSD < 3 Å). Several other ligands (L02, L05, and L07) also displayed promising profiles. Most compounds complied with Lipinski's rule of five and showed acceptable predicted ADMET properties. These preliminary findings suggest that Rhizophora mucronate -derived phytochemicals, particularly L10, are promising candidates for further experimental evaluation as modulators of Keap1 and YEATS2 in lung cancer. This study provides a computational framework for prioritizing natural product leads from mangrove species for subsequent in vitro and in vivo validation.

papers.authors_conclusion: 我们提出，可塑性最宜被理解为一种耦联的调控状态，源于致癌背景、染色质控制与代谢支持之间的相互作用；界定这些依赖如何产生并在高可塑性过渡态中形成功能耦联，应有助于识别在替代谱系程序稳定之前拦截谱系转换的切入点。

papers.abstract_en: Cellular plasticity is a central feature of malignant progression, allowing tumour cells to change identity during tumour evolution, therapeutic adaptation, and metastatic dissemination. This issue is especially acute in lung cancer, where the respiratory epithelium is intrinsically permissive to cell-state change. Genetic lesions, chromatin regulation, and metabolic adaptation are often framed as parallel determinants of lineage plasticity. Emerging evidence instead points to functional coupling across these layers. Oncogenic alterations can weaken lineage fidelity and open alternative trajectories, chromatin regulators can stabilise transitional states and enforce new transcriptional programmes, and metabolic rewiring can supply the biochemical conditions required for these states to emerge and persist. Microenvironmental cues further influence which trajectories are selected and maintained. Here, we discuss the genetic, epigenetic, and metabolic determinants of lineage plasticity in lung cancer, focusing on the points at which they intersect. We propose that plasticity is most usefully understood as a coupled regulatory state, arising from the interaction between oncogenic context, chromatin control, and metabolic support. Defining how these dependencies arise and become functionally coupled within high-plasticity transitional states should help identify points at which lineage switching can be intercepted before alternative lineage programmes are stabilised.

papers.abstract_en: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains the most aggressive form of breast cancer with a worse prognosis than other subtypes. Its high metastatic potential, limited availability of targeted therapies, and increased likelihood of being diagnosed at an advanced stage make it one of the most complex clinical challenges in breast cancer. Today, thanks to the advent of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), clinical outcomes have improved significantly. In this context, sacituzumab govitecan (SG) has been a true revolution. The case reported here illustrates how this therapeutic opportunity produced lasting clinical benefit in a highly complex patient with a triple neoplasm at presentation: inoperable locally advanced TNBC, operable colon cancer, and localized lung cancer. The chemorefractory patient (rapid progression of the first two lines of chemotherapy) received SG as a third-line treatment, showing a sustained response lasting more than 12 months and a significant benefit in terms of quality of life. This case highlights how a proper multidisciplinary approach can lead to a lasting clinical benefit from therapy. Deviating from the cases reported in clinical studies, it is important to underscore how, in this context, clinical choice prevailed. Given the locally advanced stage of the breast cancer, characterized by carcinomatous mastitis tending to ulceration and the high proliferation rate, compared to the localized stage of lung adenocarcinoma, a multidisciplinary decision was made to treat the more rapidly progressing disease, TNBC. In light of this, the importance of collecting clinical practice data to support the complex challenges we face daily is emphasized.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between the lung and bronchus cancer incidence rate, the lung and bronchus cancer mortality rate, economic growth, health expenditures, and environmental degradation using data from US states. METHODS: In the study, the cointegration and causality relationships among the time series data were examined. The autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) bounds test was used to estimate the short- and long-term coefficients of the variables representing lung and bronchus cancer incidence bronchus and mortality rates, economic growth, health expenditures, and environmental degradation variables. The data used in the study cover the annual period from 1999 through 2020. RESULTS: According to the ARDL bounds test results, economic growth and environmental degradation increased lung and bronchus cancer incidence mortality rates, while health expenditures reduced them. Causality tests indicated that economic growth unidirectionally affected lung and bronchus cancer incidence and mortality rates and environmental degradation. The results of other causality tests are presented in the conclusion section. CONCLUSION: Based on the findings, it is recommended to implement policies that reduce environmental degradation without hindering economic growth. By implementing such policies, cancer incidence and mortality rates may decrease, and at the same time, public welfare may increase. Policymakers should make decisions that advance both economic and human health objectives.

papers.abstract_en: We present the case of a woman in her 30s presenting in the second trimester with frank haematuria and left flank discomfort. MRI revealed a T3b bladder tumour with suspected peritoneal invasion. Chemotherapy was contraindicated due to teratogenicity. A coordinated obstetrics-urology MDT was undertaken at 33 weeks, an elective caesarean section was performed immediately followed by a transurethral resection of bladder for tumour debulking and histological assessment. A preterm but healthy infant was delivered and subsequently discharged from NICU. Histology revealed grade 2 bladder adenocarcinoma, in keeping with urachal origin. The patient progressed to metastatic T4 disease with pulmonary metastases and peritoneal involvement, requiring palliative chemotherapy. This case underscores the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in managing advanced bladder cancer during pregnancy, balancing maternal and foetal safety, respecting patient preferences and optimising oncological outcomes while highlighting the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of cancer diagnosis in pregnancy.

papers.abstract_en: A man in his late 70s presented with progressive, painless scrotal swelling. The initial ultrasound was reported as a simple hydrocele, and he was scheduled for surgery. At operation, friable nodules on the tunica vaginalis were biopsied, confirming malignant epithelioid mesothelioma. Staging CT showed no pleural or peritoneal disease, supporting a primary tunica vaginalis origin. As the tunica vaginalis is an embryological continuation of the peritoneum, it is exceptionally rare for mesothelioma to arise here as a true primary rather than as a secondary spread from the peritoneum. This case highlights a rare primary malignant mesothelioma masquerading as a hydrocele, the limitations of ultrasound as a sole diagnostic tool and the importance of maintaining suspicion when operative findings are discordant with imaging.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy with high linear energy transfer (LET) has shown promise for improving cancer outcomes. Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) combines charged-particle dose conformality with enhanced biological effectiveness. However, clinical development remains constrained by limited center availability, modest trial accrual, and few randomized studies. We reviewed the global landscape of CIRT studies open to enrollment to identify current priorities and gaps. METHODS: This Particle Therapy Cooperative Group (PTCOG)-sanctioned project, conducted within the CIRT Guidelines Subcommittee, identified studies through registry review and institutional verification. ClinicalTrials.gov and the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials were searched from December 2025 through February 2026. We included interventional CIRT trials and prospective registries open to new enrollment and excluded studies not open to enrollment, retrospective cohorts, proton-only studies, and preclinical studies. RESULTS: Thirty-six studies were identified: 35 interventional trials in 6 countries and 1 North American registry-based comparative-effectiveness study. Japan had the largest share, followed by Germany, China, Italy, Austria, and France. Three centers (SPHIC, QST, and HIT) accounted for 21 of 36 studies. The portfolio included 7 phase I, 23 phase II, 5 phase III, and 1 registry study. Pancreatic cancer and sarcoma-related tumors each accounted for 7 studies; head and neck cancers, 5; prostate and breast cancers, 3 each; glioblastoma, lung cancer, and gynecologic malignancies, 2 each; and mucosal melanoma, mixed solid tumors, kidney cancer, esophageal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma, 1 each. Most studies were conducted at a single institution and emphasized feasibility, toxicity, local control, progression-free survival, or overall survival. CONCLUSIONS: This expert-verified inventory shows that CIRT studies open to enrollment remain concentrated by center, disease site, and phase. Future progress may depend more on shared outcome definitions, transparent biological dose reporting, and registry-enabled or multicenter comparative designs than on additional isolated single-institution studies.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) requires accurate subtyping for prognosis and treatment, yet conventional histopathology is time-consuming and subjective. This study applies label-free multiphoton microscopy (MPM) to quantify extracellular matrix remodeling, imaging collagen via SHG and elastin via TPEF in 88 specimens from 72 patients. We introduce a SHG/TPEF ratio (STR) system to assess tumor invasiveness. Results show progressive "fiber desertification," reduced fiber content, and decreased collagen alignment in high-grade LUAD subtypes. STR metrics strongly correlate with pathological grading and effectively distinguish aggressive patterns. This MPM-based framework enables rapid, objective intraoperative identification of high-grade LUAD, improving diagnostic precision and clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Although prior reports suggest sickle cell disease (SCD) as a risk factor for lead poisoning, this association remains understudied. This paper assesses the relationship between SCD and elevated blood lead levels (BLLs) in New York City children. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective matched cohort study of children born in NYC from 2004 to 2016 and tested for BLLs from 2004 to 2022. Children with SCD were matched 1:2 to children without SCD based on maternal race and country of birth. Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression estimated associations between SCD and BLLs ≥3.5, ≥5, ≥10, and ≥15 µg/dL, adjusting for Medicaid status, housing age, and maternal race. Additional analyses evaluated effect modification by age and SCD genotype. RESULTS: The cohort included 1463 children with SCD and 2982 without SCD. SCD was associated with lower odds of BLLs ≥3.5 µg/dL (odds ratio [OR] 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.66-0.99), no difference at ≥5 µg/dL (OR 0.86; 95% CI: 0.66-1.10), and higher odds at ≥10 µg/dL (OR 1.82; 95% CI: 1.06-3.13), with a similar estimate at ≥15 µg/dL (OR 2.23; 95% CI: 0.98-5.07). The SCD-by-age interaction was significant at ≥10 µg/dL (OR 4.47; 95% CI: 1.41-15.50), and children with HbSS had significantly higher odds of BLLs ≥10 µg/dL and BLLs ≥15 µg/dL than children without SCD (OR 2.25 and 2.98, respectively). CONCLUSION: Children with SCD have increased odds of elevated BLLs at higher thresholds, especially those aged ≥3 years and those with HbSS. Targeted rescreening of these children warrants consideration.

papers.abstract_en: Human orphan genes are poorly annotated and lowly expressed, which makes their behavior in disease difficult to establish. We analyzed paired normal and disease RNA-seq libraries from four cohorts, quantified against a combined reference in which 2190 of 198,507 transcripts are orphan. Cohorts were first screened for library-level differences between the two conditions, and one (GSE40419, lung adenocarcinoma) was excluded because sequencing depth, pseudoalignment rate, and submission provenance all differed by condition; it is retained throughout as a calibration. In the remaining three cohorts, comprising 151 matched pairs from psoriasis, laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma, we measured the change in the fraction of transcripts with zero abundance, a quantity that does not depend on any transformation of expression. Orphan transcripts lose detection relative to non-orphan transcripts matched on abundance and on cross-patient detection frequency, by +0.0250±0.0178, +0.0553±0.0073, and +0.0659±0.0122 once the global shift in detection is held fixed. The three estimates are homogeneous (p=0.163) and pool to +0.0544±0.0059, whereas the same analysis applied to the excluded cohort returns thirteen times that value. We report the result at the level at which it is measured, and withdraw the patient-level and cohort-specific claims made in the first preprint version of this work.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate documentation of critical intraoperative oncologic findings is essential for the subsequent management of children with solid tumors. This program of research aimed to establish an evidence-informed framework for operative documentation and evaluate whether synoptic reporting improves documentation completeness compared with traditional narrative reporting. A sequential, multiphase translational program of research was undertaken. First, evidence-based surgical guidelines for Wilms tumor and rhabdomyosarcoma were developed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework to identify surgical factors relevant to local control and subsequent treatment. These recommendations informed an international multidisciplinary Delphi consensus process to establish essential universal and tumor-specific intraoperative reporting elements and develop a standardized synoptic operative reporting template. The template was subsequently implemented across five pediatric oncology centers in a prospective before-and-after study. The primary outcome was complete documentation of six predefined critical intraoperative oncologic elements. Exploratory end-user feedback assessed usability and acceptability. The guideline development process generated evidence-based recommendations addressing key aspects of pediatric solid tumor surgery, including lymph node sampling, vascular involvement, surgical margins, tumor spillage, and residual disease. The International Delphi consensus subsequently established 15 consensus statements defining essential operative documentation, including universal and tumor-specific elements. Following implementation of synoptic reporting, complete documentation of all six predefined critical intraoperative elements increased from 3 of 73 narrative reports (4.1%) to 71 of 92 synoptic reports (77.2%), an absolute increase of 73.1 percentage points (p < 0.000001). Exploratory end-user evaluation demonstrated high perceived usability, with a mean System Usability Scale score of 81.1. This translational program establishes an evidence-informed framework for operative documentation in pediatric surgical oncology by linking evidence-based guideline development, international consensus, and implementation of a standardized synoptic reporting tool. Synoptic reporting substantially improved the completeness of documentation of critical intraoperative oncologic findings compared with narrative reporting.

papers.abstract_en: Longer Barrett esophagus (BE) segments are associated with worse outcomes than shorter segments. However, it remains uncertain whether BE length is still a clinically actionable variable in modern surveillance, risk stratification, and treatment pathways. We reviewed current literature on the relevance of BE length as a predictor of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) severity, cancer risk, treatment outcomes, regression after treatment, and remission after ablation. BE length correlates with hiatal hernia size, esophageal dysmotility, esophagitis, and acid exposure time. Long-segment BE carries a greater risk of dysplasia or progression to esophageal adenocarcinoma than short-segment BE, although smaller segments are not risk-free. Longer BE length was associated with treatment failure and increased post-treatment pain. BE length also predicted recurrence of BE, dysplasia, or adenocarcinoma after endoscopic ablation therapy. In conclusion, most current studies report BE outcomes without stratifying results by length. BE length, however, functions as a continuous clinical variable that influences multiple aspects of care, including progression risk, surveillance intervals, treatment complexity, likelihood of eradication, recurrence after therapy, and incorporation into emerging prediction models. In other words, the contemporary importance of length lies less in preserving a historical cutoff than in recognizing length as one component of multidimensional risk stratification.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is an aggressive malignancy with dismal clinical outcomes, and how cellular senescence modulates ESCC biology remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomic profiles from the TCGA-ESCC cohort with a curated panel of cellular senescence-related genes to identify and functionally validate senescence-associated regulators in ESCC. Univariate Cox regression and consensus clustering stratified ESCC patients into two molecular subtypes with divergent survival. Through differential expression analysis, random forest prioritization, and independent validation in the GSE20347 cohort, we identified GREM2 and PIK3C2G as lead candidate genes. Both were consistently downregulated in ESCC tumors and cell lines, and low expression predicted poorer overall survival. papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Transient elastography may overestimate fibrosis in autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) because hepatic inflammation independently increases liver stiffness measurement (LSM). We aimed to determine which inflammation markers confound LSM in AIH, whether algebraic correction improves accuracy, and when LSM becomes reliable for fibrosis staging. METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort of adults with AIH, paired diagnostic Metavir biopsy, and at least one FibroScan visit with same-visit alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and immunoglobulin G (IgG). Mixed-effects linear regression modeled LSM on biopsy stage, ALT, IgG, and time since diagnosis with a patient-level random intercept. An inflammation-adjusted LSM was computed by subtracting estimated ALT and IgG contributions. Spearman correlation and DeLong-tested AUROC for advanced fibrosis (F3-F4) compared measured and adjusted LSM, stratified by inflammation state and treatment timing. RESULTS: We analyzed 208 FibroScan observations from 119 AIH patients (49 with advanced fibrosis). IgG was independently associated with LSM (β = +0.003 kPa per mg/dL, p < 0.001) while ALT was not (β ≈ 0, p = 0.68). The IgG-LSM relationship varied by treatment timing (IgG × 0-6 months interaction p = 0.001; IgG × 12-24 months p = 0.004). Algebraic correction did not improve discrimination (full-cohort AUROC measured 0.76 vs adjusted 0.72, DeLong p = 0.18). LSM accuracy for advanced fibrosis varied by timing: AUROC 0.71 pretreatment (n = 35), 0.64 at 12-24 months (n = 22), and 0.83 beyond 24 months (n = 72). CONCLUSIONS: In AIH, IgG-not ALT-independently inflates LSM, with a time-dependent effect strongest early after diagnosis. Algebraic correction did not improve fibrosis discrimination, but LSM accuracy improved substantially beyond 24 months after AIH diagnosis. Timing rather than algebraic correction is the more actionable clinical strategy for FibroScan interpretation in AIH.

papers.abstract_en: Standard management guidelines generally recommend immunosuppressive therapy (IST) as first-line treatment for older patients with severe aplastic anemia (SAA), whereas the role of upfront haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (haplo-HSCT) in this population remains uncertain, particularly in patients with complex comorbidities. We report a 62-year-old woman with SAA, a history of surgically resected stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, and previous left lower extremity deep vein thrombosis treated with venous stent implantation and long-term aspirin therapy. Because no matched sibling or unrelated donor was available, and following individualized counseling regarding IST and transplantation, the patient underwent upfront haplo-HSCT combined with umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells after a conditioning regimen including fludarabine, busulfan, cyclophosphamide, antithymocyte globulin, and thiotepa. Neutrophil engraftment occurred on post-transplant day +12, and platelet independence was achieved on day +13. Donor chimerism reached 99.6% by day +14 and remained within the complete-chimerism range through the latest available assessment in January 2026. In late December 2025 and January 2026, the patient developed cytomegalovirus infection accompanied by transient trilineage cytopenia; after anti-CMV treatment with maribavir, the infection was controlled and peripheral blood counts subsequently recovered. At the most recent clinical follow-up on August 6, 2026, approximately 17 months after transplantation, no chronic graft-versus-host disease had developed, the previous lung adenocarcinoma remained in remission, and the thrombotic condition remained clinically stable. This case suggests that upfront haplo-HSCT combined with UC-MSCs may represent a feasible individualized treatment option for carefully selected older patients with SAA who lack matched donors, although broader conclusions require larger studies and longer follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) can show declining age-standardized rates while the number of affected people grows. We quantified this divergence and its demographic and socioeconomic pattern across Asia. METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease 2023 estimates for 48 Asian locations (2009-2023), primary analyses examined incidence, prevalence, deaths, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), age-sex patterns, estimated annual percentage changes, demographic decomposition, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI)-related inequality. Exploratory analyses assessed pre-2020 trend deviations and subregional ARIMA forecasts to 2030. RESULTS: From 2009 to 2023, incident cases increased from 7.74 million to 10.75 million (38.9%), prevalent cases from 91.88 million to 129.76 million (41.2%), deaths from 2.11 million to 2.63 million (24.8%), and DALYs from 46.43 million to 55.97 million (20.5%). Age-standardized incidence and prevalence rates declined in 34 of 48 locations, death rates in 37, and DALY rates in 43. Of 522,061 additional deaths, population growth contributed 345,084 and population aging 933,776, partly offset by epidemiological change (-756,799). The death-rate SII changed from -69.90 in 2009 to -87.22 in 2023, and the concentration index from -0.140 to -0.220, indicating increasing concentration in lower-SDI populations. Summed subregional point deviations for 2020-2023 were small relative to expected burden: deaths were 0.57% and DALYs 0.26% above expected, whereas incidence was 0.35% and prevalence 0.51% below expected. Conditional 2030 point forecasts were 13.28 million incident cases, 156.74 million prevalent cases, 2.81 million deaths, and 62.63 million DALYs. CONCLUSION: Declining age-standardized rates have not reduced COPD service need across Asia. Population aging and lower-SDI disadvantage support prevention and care strategies tailored to demographic and socioeconomic context.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Patients with cancer experience nutrition challenges, but access to registered dietitians (RDs) is limited. The purpose of this study was to determine whether a specialized Artificial Intelligence (AI) Nutrition Platform trained on curated high-quality evidence is equivalent in providing nutrition information to patients with cancer compared with oncology-credentialed RDs. METHODS: Twenty nutrition queries were developed by an expert panel, encompassing common cancer types, symptoms, and food allergies/preferences. These queries were administered to the AI Platform and to four nationally recruited human dietitians. Three expert reviewers with >10 years of cancer-specific nutrition experience blindly reviewed all query responses using a modified version of the Quality Assessment of Medical AI (mQAMAI) instrument, which assigns a score between 1 and 5 for accuracy, clarity, relevance, completeness, and usefulness (total quality score between 5 and 25). The primary outcome was mQAMAI total score. Equivalence was evaluated a priori using two one-sided tests (TOST). Secondary outcomes included readability and response time. RESULTS: The AI Nutrition Platform met equivalence criteria with human dietitians at ±3 to ±5 points (mean difference: 0.9 points; 90% CI, -0.27 to 2.15; TOST P < .05), while scoring higher on individual components: clarity (4.2 v 3.9; P = .001), relevance (4.1 v 3.9; P = .04), and usefulness (3.8 v 3.5; P = .02). AI responses were easier to read (Flesch-Kincaid grade level 7.2 v 9.8; P < .001) with faster response time (8.5 v 18.5 minutes per two queries; P < .001). CONCLUSION: The AI Platform was equivalent to human dietitians for cancer nutrition information, delivering responses with greater clarity, relevance, usefulness, and readability in less time. This tool could broaden access to nutrition support for patients in settings where access to dietitians is limited.

This higher-risk subgroup warrants specific pulmonary vascular evaluation and tighter clinical follow-up.

The results point to an increasingly complex genetic testing profile in healthcare along with a widening gap in application. Further research into genomics implementation is required to fully realise the benefits of genetics and genomics testing.

Twelve patients (44%) had ≤ 1.5 cm2 residual tumor. Seventeen patients (63%) required ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement. Seven (26%) developed postoperative complications. Ten tumors were of classic histology, eight desmoplastic, six anaplastic, and three MBEN. Sixteen tumors (59%) were molecularly subgrouped: SHH (fourteen), Group-3 (two). Patients received various treatment protocols: HeadStart 1&2-like protocols (seventeen), SKK-92 (eight), and BBSFOP (two). Although 21 patients were planned for autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT), only 13 received it (three received SKK-92 due to financial constraints, two prematurely stopped therapy, two developed early tumor progression, and one shifted to BBSFOP protocol due to chemotherapy toxicity). At a median follow-up of 7.4 years (range, 2.5-16 years), 17 patients (63%) are alive. Twelve patients (44%) are alive in CR1 without radiotherapy (five of whom also avoided ASCT), three in CR2 after CSI-36 Gy, one in CR3 after ASCT then CSI-23.4 Gy, and one patient lost to follow-up after salvage CSI-36 Gy. Two patients developed secondary tumors: one died from high-grade glioma and one developed thyroid carcinoma. Two survivors needed cataract surgery, and four had hearing loss. Ten survivors need hormonal supplements. CONCLUSIONS: Some infants and young children with medulloblastoma can achieve durable cure without ACST or radiotherapy, even in LMICs. While these therapies remain critical salvage options, lifelong comprehensive support is imperative to optimize survival and quality of life.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) is a life-threatening complication of pediatric acute leukemia. However, whether early-onset ICH and late-onset ICH are distinct clinical entities remains unclear. This study investigated the characteristics, neuroimaging findings, and outcomes of ICH. METHODS: Children with newly diagnosed acute leukemia were retrospectively reviewed. Patients with ICH were significantly younger and more frequently had KMT2A rearrangements, hyperleukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and coagulation abnormalities than those without ICH. Patients with ICH had a significantly lower 5-year OS rate than those without ICH (55.4% vs. 90.4%, p < 0.001). Early-onset ICH predominantly occurred in patients with acute myeloid leukemia, and it was characterized by multifocal hemorrhages at presentation. Late-onset ICH occurred exclusively in patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Three infants with KMT2A-rearranged B-cell ALL developed marked cerebral atrophy, followed by subdural hematoma. Five patients required neurosurgical intervention, and all survivors had persistent neurological sequelae. CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric acute leukemia, ICH comprises two clinically distinct patterns. Early-onset ICH is primarily associated with leukemia-related coagulopathy. Late-onset ICH is characterized by cerebral atrophy, followed by subdural hematoma, in infants with KMT2A-rearranged B-cell ALL. Recognizing these distinct patterns may lead to earlier diagnosis, neuroimaging evaluation, and timely neurosurgical intervention.

Decentralized screening programs, in which referring providers manage eligibility identification, referrals, and follow-up without dedicated coordination infrastructure, are common across clinical settings. Yet the relationship between program design and delivery outcomes in decentralized contexts has received little attention. This study examined how a decentralized lung cancer screening program delivered screening across each step of the pathway, from patient identification through annual follow-up. The goal was to identify where and how program design produced gaps in delivery from the perspectives of patients and providers.MethodsThis qualitative study used semi-structured interviews conducted between July 2023 and May 2024 at an academic medical center in Alabama as part of a larger explanatory sequential mixed methods study. Fifteen patients who had completed screening and six providers representing primary care, pulmonology, and radiology participated. Interviews explored screening awareness, decision-making, and program delivery processes. Transcripts were analyzed using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and constant comparative method. Reporting followed the COREQ guideline.ResultsDelivery failures were structural and concentrated at the front end of the screening pathway. Eligibility identification depended on incidental patient exposure rather than systematic outreach. Referrals reflected individual provider initiative rather than standardized workflows. Result tracking and nodule follow-up fell to ordering providers without dedicated support. Coverage gaps and geographic distance compounded these determinants.ConclusionReduced uptake in this decentralized program pointed largely to structural barriers. Closing the implementation gap may require program design changes and proactive outreach that does not depend on the clinical encounter to begin.

papers.abstract_en: Gallbladder necrosis is a rare but life-threatening complication of acute cholecystitis, likely resulting from chronic blood flow, inflammation, and intraluminal pressure. It most commonly occurs in elderly or critically ill patients with significant comorbidities and is often underreported due to its nonspecific presentation. This diagnosis is usually associated with right upper quadrant pain, leukocytosis, and fever. Here, we present an 80-year-old woman with metastatic lung cancer, COPD, and an extensive surgical and oncologic history who was incidentally found to have radiographic findings concerning for gangrenous cholecystitis but remained asymptomatic. Despite these findings, the patient remained clinically stable with improving leukocytosis during her inpatient course and was managed conservatively without surgical intervention. Post-discharge follow-up was unavailable.

papers.abstract_en: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with a complex pathogenesis, necessitating the development of safe and effective therapeutic interventions. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of Aucubin (Auc) against dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced UC in mice. Using a DSS-induced colitis model, we systematically evaluated the multifaceted effects of Auc by assessing the Disease Activity Index (DAI), colon length, histopathological changes, immunohistochemical staining, ELISA results, proteomic profiles, 16S rRNA sequencing data, and untargeted metabolomic analyses. Compared with the DSS group, Aucubin high-dose (Auc-H, 100 mg/kg) treatment significantly attenuated DSS-induced body weight loss, DAI score elevation, and colon shortening (all p < 0.05). The therapeutic efficacy of Auc-H was comparable to that of the positive control drug 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA). Mechanistically, Auc restored intestinal barrier integrity by stimulating mucin 2 (Muc2) secretion and upregulating the expression of zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) and Occludin, which in turn significantly reduced serum lipopolysaccharide (LPS) concentrations (p < 0.001). Proteomic analysis identified 2180 DSS-induced differentially expressed proteins, of which 679 were significantly counter-regulated by Auc-H, mainly involving the complement and coagulation cascades and immune-inflammatory pathways. Furthermore, gut microbiota analysis showed that Auc promoted the growth of beneficial bacteria, improving microbial balance. Untargeted metabolomics further revealed that Auc-H significantly restored the levels of 120 DSS-induced differential metabolites, including 86 upregulated and 34 downregulated metabolites, among which were protective tryptophan-derived indole metabolites (p < 0.05). Consequently, Aucubin exhibits significant clinical potential in alleviating UC via a multifaceted mechanism. These effects include reduced inflammation, restored epithelial barrier integrity, and modulated microbial metabolism. These findings provide crucial experimental evidence supporting the potential application of Auc as a preventive therapy for UC.

papers.abstract_en: Protein S-palmitoylation provides a key regulatory mechanism for diverse cellular activities. Although palmitoylated proteins are frequently observed in cholesterol-enriched membrane microdomains, how protein palmitoylation reciprocally regulates cholesterol metabolism remains elusive. Here, we identify DHHC13 as a critical regulator linking protein palmitoylation to lysosomal cholesterol egress. Through an shRNA screen, we found that lack of DHHC13 led to pronounced lysosomal cholesterol accumulation. Mechanistically, DHHC13 directly palmitoylated Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Loss of palmitoylation disrupted NPC1 association with lysosomes and caused its degradation, thereby impairing lysosomal cholesterol egress. Dhhc13 -/- mice phenocopied Npc1 -/- mice, displaying cholesterol deposition in the brain, liver, spleen, and kidney, along with significant Purkinje cell loss. Furthermore, two clinically relevant DHHC13 mutants (Q173H and R451Q) associated with neurodegenerative disorders showed diminished catalytic activity and failed to restore NPC1 palmitoylation or lysosomal cholesterol egress. Collectively, our findings uncover DHHC13 as a critical regulator of lysosomal cholesterol metabolism via NPC1 palmitoylation, providing mechanistic insights into cholesterol-related neurological disorders.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) incidence is rising globally, and current therapeutic options carry substantial morbidity and mortality. We report the feasibility and early outcomes of knife-assisted endoscopic full-thickness resection (kFTR) as a palliative local control in nonsurgical candidates. METHODS: Three patients with suspected locally advanced distal EAC (clinical tumor stage T1b-T2), no nodal or distant disease, and high Charlson Comorbidity Index scores were unfit for surgery and declined chemoradiotherapy. All consented to kFTR: a submucosal pocket was created cranial to the suspected invasive area, the muscle-retracting sign was identified, and the muscularis propria was incised to access the periesophageal space. The lesion was dissected laterally and resected en bloc. A fully covered metal stent was then placed. RESULTS: Patients resumed oral intake on day 5 without major adverse events. All had EAC pathologic tumor stage 1b with invasion into the deepest layer of the submucosa; 2 had positive vertical margins. One remained disease-free (24 months); 2 had local recurrence by 6 months but remained asymptomatic at last follow-up (10 and 14 months). CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected symptomatic, inoperable patients, kFTR achieved short-to-medium term symptom control for locally advanced EAC with acceptable safety.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Diverse oncology workforces improve care quality, patient satisfaction, and outcomes, particularly among underserved populations. This study aimed to evaluate long-term demographic and educational trends among U.S. cancer-related medical trainees and examine how these trends have shifted across specialties over a 15-year period. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Publicly available data were sourced from the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Data Resource Books. Gender and educational-background trends were evaluated from 2007-2023, while race/ethnicity trends were evaluated from 2011-2023 across cancer-related physician training programs, including hematology-medical oncology, medical oncology, radiation oncology, surgical oncology, pediatric hematology-oncology, medical genetics, pathology, diagnostic and interventional radiology, and nuclear medicine. Demographic variables included gender, race/ethnicity, and age; educational background was categorized as U.S. allopathic, U.S. osteopathic, or international medical graduate (IMG). Trends were assessed using the nonparametric Mann-Kendall test, with P<.05 indicating statistical significance. RESULTS: Between 2007 and 2023, female trainee representation rose significantly (47.0% to 51.5%; p<0.001), with notable gains in pediatric hematology-oncology and medical oncology. Hispanic/Latino representation increased significantly from 7.9% to 11.6% overall (p<0.001), while African American/Black representation remained unchanged (7.1% to 7.5%; p>0.05). Asian/Pacific Islander proportions rose in select specialties. The percentage of U.S. osteopathic graduates increased across most specialties (5.1% to 16.2%; p<0.001), whereas IMG representation declined slightly overall. U.S. allopathic representation decreased from 62.9% to 53.3% (p<0.001), with variation across specialties. CONCLUSION: While gains in gender and Hispanic/Latino representation are evident, African American/Black trainee representation remains stagnant, and changes in IMG participation vary across specialties. These diverging trends highlight persistent representation gaps within the U.S. cancer workforce training pipeline. Continued monitoring will be important to determine how evolving educational and accreditation policies influence these trends over time. POLICY SUMMARY: Based on these findings, program directors and professional societies should maintain inclusive recruitment practices and continue systematic monitoring of workforce diversity as accreditation policies evolve. Sustained institutional commitment may help preserve patient trust, address workforce needs, and support an oncology workforce that better reflects the populations it serves.

papers.abstract_en: Tetrandrine (TET) is a bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloid with promising anticancer activity, although its limited selectivity toward malignant over non-cancerous cells restricts its therapeutic potential. A series of mono- and bis-N-substituted tetrandrine derivatives was therefore investigated to determine whether N-functionalization could improve the cytotoxic selectivity of the parent scaffold. The series included the two new compounds MU1NT and DPBT. Following initial screening in non-cancerous ARPE-19 retinal epithelial cells, selected derivatives were evaluated against 22Rv1 prostate carcinoma, A549 lung adenocarcinoma, MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer, HCT-116 colorectal carcinoma, and HeLa cervical cancer cells. TET exhibited broad but poorly selective cytotoxicity, with IC50 values of 6.81 ± 1.79 and 6.00 ± 1.96 μM in ARPE-19 and 22Rv1 cells, respectively, corresponding to a selectivity index (SI) of 1.13. By contrast, DBT showed IC50 values of 45.44 ± 1.37 μM in ARPE-19 cells and 9.89 ± 1.08 μM in 22Rv1 cells, with an SI of 4.59, the highest experimentally determined value among the tetrandrine-based compounds evaluated. MU1NT also displayed improved selectivity toward 22Rv1 cells (SI = 2.57), although with lower cytotoxic potency than DBT. Fluorescence microscopy using DAPI and phalloidin revealed pronounced nuclear and cytoskeletal alterations in DBT-treated 22Rv1 cells, whereas ARPE-19 morphology was comparatively preserved. Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry further demonstrated an apoptosis-associated response in 22Rv1 cells, with total apoptosis reaching 86.30 ± 1.27% for TET and 34.77 ± 5.13% for DBT after 24 h at their respective MTT-derived IC50 concentrations. Molecular docking suggested distinct predicted interaction profiles for TET and DBT across the apoptosis-related proteins evaluated. Targeted redocking of co-crystallized venetoclax validated the Bcl-2 site-specific protocol (RMSD = 0.55 Å); however, both alkaloids scored less favorably than venetoclax, and the small score difference between TET and DBT did not account for their distinct cellular selectivity profiles. Collectively, these findings identify DBT as a promising tetrandrine derivative with improved selectivity, warranting further mechanistic studies and in vivo evaluation in prostate cancer models.

papers.abstract_en: Although expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) endografts provide excellent mechanical exclusion of aneurysm blood flow, they remain biologically inert and lack surface functions that actively prevent bacterial colonization or promote favorable graft-vessel interface responses following implantation. Here, we report a dual-functional hydrogel coating for ePTFE vascular grafts that integrates antibacterial protection with localized procoagulant activity at the graft-vessel interface. The coating, denoted as ZnO@CH, is prepared via in situ photopolymerization of methacryloyl-modified chitosan (CSMA) incorporating zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles, forming a stable, spatially confined functional layer on the outer surface of ePTFE grafts. In vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrate that the coating exhibits potent broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus while maintaining cytocompatibility with vascular endothelial cells. The ZnO@CH hydrogel promoted localized thrombus formation in a rat abdominal aorta model. Separately, an in vitro liquid-barrier assay showed that hydrogel-coated ePTFE retained its barrier function under the tested conditions. Systemic safety assessments in rodent models reveal no significant acute or chronic toxicity. Collectively, this dual-functional coating strategy offers a promising biomaterial approach for improving the biological performance of ePTFE vascular grafts.

papers.abstract_en: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, immune-mediated disease whose incidence and prevalence have continued to rise, yet little is known about how public awareness has evolved alongside clinical progress. We used Google Trends, a freely available tool that indexes the relative popularity of search queries from 0 to 100, to examine interest in the terms 'eosinophilic esophagitis' and 'EoE' in the United States from January 2004 through December 2025, and to compare the disease term with searches for regulatory-approved EoE-relevant therapies (dupilumab/Dupixent, budesonide/Eohilia, and budesonide/Jorveza) in the United States and worldwide (English-language). Search interest for 'eosinophilic esophagitis' rose substantially across two decades (+2.97 points/year; P < 0.001), with segmented regression at clinical milestones showing significant slope changes at 2007, 2011, 2013, 2020, and 2024 (all P ≤ 0.04). Secondary analysis of the 'EoE' acronym corroborated these patterns, rising across the study period (+1.3 points/year; P < 0.001) with a final-year rise (+18.2 points/year). Searches for 'Dupixent' exceeded disease-term searches in both the United States and worldwide (English-language). Seasonal and monthly variation did not statistically differ. These observations illustrate how digital epidemiology has potential to serve as a low-cost barometer of disease awareness and information-seeking behavior. As patients increasingly turn from search engines to conversational artificial intelligence, these signals may evolve and further research is needed to define how digital epidemiology best be integrated with conventional epidemiologic data.

papers.abstract_en: Acrokeratosis paraneoplastica (Bazex syndrome) is a rare paraneoplastic dermatosis characterized by psoriasiform lesions predominantly affecting acral sites and is most commonly associated with squamous cell carcinomas of the upper aerodigestive tract. Cutaneous manifestations may precede the diagnosis of the underlying malignancy, making their recognition an important diagnostic clue. We report two cases of Bazex syndrome in older men presenting with characteristic acral and facial psoriasiform lesions. In both patients, skin biopsy revealed nonspecific histopathological findings, while the clinical pattern prompted investigation for an underlying malignancy. The first patient was subsequently diagnosed with metastatic oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma. In the second patient, investigation revealed two synchronous malignancies: a large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and an oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma. These cases emphasize the diagnostic value of recognizing the clinical pattern of Bazex syndrome as a marker of underlying malignancy. In patients presenting with compatible acral psoriasiform lesions, particularly older individuals with relevant cancer risk factors, this distinctive clinical pattern should prompt systematic investigation for an occult malignancy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Children's surgery is increasingly recognized as a global health priority, yet pediatric anesthesia remains comparatively under-recognized despite being essential for safe surgical and perioperative care. THE PROBLEM: Children require specialized expertise, age-appropriate equipment, reliable monitoring, oxygen, medicines, recovery, and critical care. In many low- and middle-income countries, deficiencies across these domains limit access and contribute to preventable perioperative morbidity and mortality. THE CENTRAL CLAIM: We posit that children's surgical systems cannot be strengthened without parallel investment in pediatric anesthesia systems. Pediatric anesthesia should therefore be recognized as a cross-cutting core health-system function rather than a supporting clinical specialty. EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: This perspective integrates the WHO Health Systems Building Blocks, the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery, National Surgical, Obstetric and Anesthesia Plans, the GICS Optimal Resources for Children's Surgery framework, and Donabedian's Structure-Process-Outcome model into an Integrated Pediatric Anesthesia Systems Framework (IPASF). RECOMMENDATIONS: Governments, professional societies, academic institutions, global surgery organizations, and development partners should integrate pediatric anesthesia into surgical-system planning, workforce development, financing, service delivery, quality improvement, and research. CONCLUSION: Safe and equitable children's surgery requires deliberate investment in the systems that enable safe anesthesia. The IPASF provides a practical framework for policy, implementation, education, research, and evaluation across the perioperative continuum.

papers.abstract_en: Comprehensive genomic profiling has expanded the ability to identify potentially actionable molecular alterations across cancers, but identification of an actionable finding does not ensure that a patient will receive a genomically matched therapy. Studies of precision-oncology programs and molecular tumor boards consistently demonstrate substantial attrition between treatment recommendation and treatment initiation. The reasons extend beyond molecular interpretation and include the timing of genomic profiling, clinical deterioration, geographic availability of biomarker-selected trials, insurance and financial barriers, and disparities in access to specialty cancer care. Importantly, these barriers arise after a potentially useful molecular finding has already been identified, creating a distinction between molecular actionability and practical treatment access. This commentary argues that the next implementation challenge for precision oncology is to make clinically meaningful genomic findings realistically actionable. Comprehensive genomic profiling should occur early enough to inform treatment planning; molecular tumor board recommendations should be linked to realistic treatment and trial opportunities; financial and insurance barriers should be anticipated when recommendations are made; and equity should be evaluated beyond access to testing to include receipt of genomically informed treatment. As genomic profiling becomes increasingly integrated into routine cancer care, precision oncology should be judged not only by its ability to identify therapeutic opportunities but also by whether patients can reach those opportunities while they remain clinically relevant.

papers.abstract_en: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally, with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection as the primary etiological factor. Cervical precancerous lesions, including high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and adenocarcinoma in situ, represent the critical window for intervention prior to invasive cancer development. However, additional factors such as immunosuppression, smoking, and microbiome composition also play crucial roles in the development of cervical precancerous lesions. While HPV vaccination, screening, and treatment have reduced cancer incidence, these must be complemented by personalized approaches that target the molecular mechanisms driving carcinogenesis. Key dysregulated tumor suppressors (e.g., p16) and signaling pathways (PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin) highlight the need for advanced therapeutic strategies. The immune microenvironment also plays a critical role in cancer progression, suggesting potential for immunotherapy. Promising biomarkers like p16, Ki67, and microRNAs require integration with technologies such as single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics for deeper insights into tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment dynamics. Additionally, while deep learning models hold promise in improving diagnostic accuracy for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), challenges such as data variability and interpretability need addressing. In conclusion, incorporating genomics, transcriptomics, immunotherapy, and artificial intelligence will enable more personalized and effective interventions, ultimately reducing the global burden of cervical cancer.

papers.abstract_en: Anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) is a human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cancer with a rising incidence. People living with human immunodeficiency virus (PLHIV) are at the highest risk. Recent evidence has shown that treatment of the precursor lesion, high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), can prevent cancer development. Consequently, several countries have published screening guidelines for anal HSIL as a strategy to decrease cancer incidence. In Australia, the Australasian Society for HIV, Viral Hepatitis and Sexual Health Medicine (ASHM) has recently released guidelines for PLHIV, based on HPV testing and genotyping, with liquid-based cytology (LBC) used as a triage tool for those testing positive to high-risk HPV. The pathologist's role will be critical to the success of this endeavour. This article describes the scientific basis for the recommended screening algorithm. The key features of each testing component are outlined, including anal swab collection, biopsy interpretation and the importance of relevant clinical information, to enhance communication between pathologist and clinician. Future developments are discussed, including the possibility of extension of the benefits of such screening to other at-risk groups.

papers.abstract_en: Iron-driven reactive oxygen species (ROS) amplification forms a self-sustaining pathological cycle in Parkinson's disease (PD), yet remains difficult to therapeutically interrupt due to the lack of strategies that coordinate metal homeostasis and redox regulation. Here, we report an electronic-structure-engineered nanoregulatory strategy that regulates the iron-ROS cycle rather than passively scavenging ROS. Nitrogen-doped, herbal-derived carbon dots (CD) were rationally constructed to establish a conjugated electronic framework, in which heteroatom-induced electron delocalization defined redox-active sites and governed the coupling between iron chelation and catalytic ROS regulation. This structure-electronic state-function relationship enabled programmable disruption of the iron-ROS feedback loop at its source. Functionally, the nanoregulators achieved low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1)-mediated brain delivery, exhibited efficient central nervous system exposure, and underwent brain clearance via the cerebrospinal fluid pathway. At the cellular level, they restored mitochondrial function, suppressed ferroptosis-associated lipid peroxidation, and reprogramed stress-related pathways toward neuronal survival. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed coordinated regulation of redox, metabolic, and inflammatory networks. In Parkinsonian mice, this strategy reduced iron deposition, preserved dopaminergic neurons, and improved motor function. Integration with levodopa further enabled sustained, disease-modifying neuroprotection.

papers.abstract_en: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators of gene expression involved in immune homeostasis, inflammation, fibrosis, and vascular remodeling. Their dysregulation has been increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis of autoimmune connective tissue diseases (ACTDs). Recent studies have identified numerous differentially expressed miRNAs associated with immune dysregulation and progressive tissue injury in these disorders. This review summarizes current evidence on the pathogenic roles of miRNAs in ACTDs, including systemic sclerosis (SSc), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), dermatomyositis (DM), Sjögren's syndrome (SS), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). In SSc, miR-145 promotes myofibroblast differentiation and contributes to fibrosis, whereas miR-21a-5p overexpression is associated with increased numbers of cells producing proinflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-17. In MCTD, preliminary studies have identified associations between miRNA-related alterations and immune or inflammatory pathways, including genetic variation involving miR-146a and exploratory changes in miR-155 expression. However, current evidence remains limited and associative and does not establish definitive roles for these miRNAs in MCTD pathogenesis. In DM, miR-125a-3p, miR-1246, and miR-3614-5p have been associated with dysregulated autophagy and inflammatory responses. In SS, miR-181d-5p is downregulated and is negatively correlated with glandular TNF-α mRNA expression, whereas miR-150-5p plays an important role in B-cell maturation and activation. In RA, miR-124a is associated with synovial hyperplasia and increased production of inflammatory mediators, such as MCP-1, whereas reduced miR-34a expression affects Th17/Treg differentiation and is associated with structural joint damage. In SLE, dysregulation of miR-142-3p and miR-122-5p is associated with disease activity and alterations in T-cell regulation and B-cell activation. Collectively, current evidence indicates that miRNA dysregulation contributes to key immunological, inflammatory, and fibrotic processes underlying ACTDs. These findings also highlight the potential of miRNAs as biomarkers for disease monitoring and as molecular targets for the development of novel therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: First-line chemoimmunotherapy (ICI-chemo) has become the standard of care for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). However, older adults are underrepresented in pivotal trials due to strict inclusion criteria that limit participation to highly selected, fit patients. Given the limited real-world comparative data, this study aimed to determine whether older adults with ES-SCLC derive greater benefit from ICI-chemo compared with chemotherapy (chemo) alone. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study including ES-SCLC patients aged 65 years or older who started first-line ICI-chemo or chemo between January 2020 and July 2024. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to adjust for baseline confounding. The main outcome was overall survival (OS) in the IPTW population. RESULTS: In the IPTW population, median OS was significantly longer in the ICI-chemo group (14.95 months; 95% CI, 12.94-19.91) compared with chemo (10.28 months; 95% CI, 8.11-13.17; HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.48-0.91; p = 0.011). Multivariable analysis confirmed that ICI-chemo exposure was independently associated with improved OS (HR, 0.608; 95% CI, 0.440-0.841; p = 0.003). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide comparative evidence of improved survival in association with ICI-chemo compared with chemo in older adults with ES-SCLC.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Psilocybin has received increased attention as a potential therapeutic intervention, but it is unclear whether news media reporting reflects the strengths and limitations of the clinical trial evidence. OBJECTIVE: To describe the annual counts of published clinical trials of therapeutic psilocybin and contemporaneous media articles and compare tone, efficacy, and safety messaging. EVIDENCE REVIEW: This systematic review included English-language randomized and nonrandomized trials of psilocybin for clinical indications published from January 1, 2014, to October 10, 2024, and media articles describing its clinical use published from January 1, 2014, to April 22, 2025. Trials were found by searching Medline, Embase, PsycInfo, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and were characterized by design, indication, use of psychotherapy, and reporting of efficacy and safety. Media articles were found through the Factiva database and were characterized by audience, tone, indication, efficacy claim, and safety content. Data were extracted by 2 reviewers. Risk of bias for randomized clinical trials was assessed descriptively using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. FINDINGS: Annual counts of both published clinical trials (n = 70) and media reports (n = 172) increased from 2018 onward. Depression was the most common clinical indication in trials (47 [67%]) and media articles (138 [80%]), while media articles frequently referenced posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) (74 [43%]) and anxiety (72 [42%]) as clinical indications despite absent and limited trial evidence, respectively, for these conditions. Overall, 49 trials (70%) reported benefit for the primary indication; 125 media articles (73%) made at least 1 positive efficacy claim, and 122 (71%) adopted a favorable tone. Trials typically described small sample sizes of less than 100 participants (65 trials [93%]) and methodologic limitations. Overall, 31 trials (44%) reported safety outcomes, with some (24 [34%]) documenting short-term adverse events, such as transient anxiety, nausea, or headache; long-term safety was rarely assessed (4 trials [6%]). Only 51 media articles (30%) mentioned safety; when harms were discussed, potential long-term psychological risks were sometimes noted (12 articles [7%]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this systematic review of clinical trials and media articles, both reported positive effects of therapeutic psilocybin with similar frequency. Academic publications were more cautious and explicit about methodologic limitations, whereas media reports often presented benefits as established, extrapolated them to indications with little or no trial evidence, and provided less safety information. Clarifying these differences in emphasis may support more transparent public communication of indication-specific evidence and uncertainty as interest in psilocybin-assisted treatments grows.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: In metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), randomized clinical trials directly comparing androgen deprivation therapy intensification using androgen synthesis inhibitors (ASIs) vs next-generation androgen receptor inhibitors (ARIs) are lacking. OBJECTIVE: To compare the outcomes associated with ASI vs ARI intensification therapy among patients with mHSPC in community or academic clinical practices. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients diagnosed with mHSPC between February 4, 2013, and April 29, 2024, with follow-up through the July 2024 data cut, providing a median (IQR) follow-up of 25.6 (24.5-26.6) months. Patient-level data were extracted from the nationwide US-based Flatiron Health electronic health record-derived deidentified research database of community and academic practices. Patients with evidence of an mHSPC diagnosis initiating treatment with an ASI (abiraterone acetate) or ARI (apalutamide or enzalutamide) within 3 months prior to or 6 months after an mHSPC diagnosis were eligible. Patients with prior docetaxel receipt were excluded. EXPOSURE: Treatment with an ASI vs an ARI. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), defined as time in months from mHSPC diagnosis to death or censoring at last recorded activity. RESULTS: Of 3404 patients (median [IQR] age, 73 [66-80] years), 1830 received treatment with an ASI (abiraterone), and 1574 with an ARI (507 apalutamide, 1067 enzalutamide). Following inverse probability of treatment weighting, patients receiving an ARI had significantly longer OS (median, 67.9 months [95% CI, 67.5 months to not reached]) compared with patients treated with the ASI (median, 57.2 months [95% CI, 52.7-63.3 months]) (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.64-0.87]); P < .001). Results were similar in sensitivity analyses using therapy initiation as the index date (HR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.62-0.84]; P < .001) and when restricted to index dates on or after December 16, 2019 (HR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.56-0.81]; P < .001). The association was not modified by insurance status or socioeconomic status. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of 3404 patients with mHSPC, treatment intensification with an ARI was associated with significantly longer OS compared with an ASI. These findings may help guide clinical treatment selection and patient counseling. However, given conflicting clinical practice data across differing database populations, only a randomized clinical trial can definitively answer this question.
